definition_zh: 意思是；意味着；打算；平均值；中间值；刻薄的；吝啬的
definition_en: to intend or signify something; also the middle value of a set of numbers, or unkind and unwilling to spend
core_image: 一句含混的话被手指向它真正要说的那件事，旁边天平恰好停在正中
scene: 统计员把五个读数的总和除开，求出中间的那个数值。 The mean of the five readings is nine.
sceneCN: 这里指「一组数的平均值」（第 4 个义项：平均数）；句意为五个读数的平均值是九。可辨识物件：记录纸、五个读数、计算器、天平；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: To have a sense
senses.definition: to have as a meaning, said of a word, sign or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、符号或手势所具有的意思
senses.example: What does this symbol mean?
senses.exampleCN: 这个符号表示什么？
senses.why: The Old English verb mænan meant 'to intend, signify', and a word's sense is what it intends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 mænan 意为「意图、意指」，而词的意思就是它所意图的东西。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to be a sign or indication of something else
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的迹象或征兆
senses.example: A red sky at night means fair weather tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的红霞意味着明天天气晴好。
senses.why: A sign points to what it intends, so the verb extends from words to natural signs.
senses.whyCN: 符号指向它所意指之物，于是这个动词从词语扩展到自然征兆。

senses.title: To intend to do
senses.definition: to have something in mind as a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某事放在心里作为目的
senses.example: I mean to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我打算今晚把报告写完。
senses.why: Intention is the inward side of meaning: what a person means is what he intends.
senses.whyCN: 意图是「意思」的内面：一个人意指什么，就是他打算什么。

senses.title: The average of a set
senses.definition: the value obtained by adding all the numbers and dividing by how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 把全部数值相加再除以个数所得的值
senses.example: Add the values and divide by five to get the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些值相加再除以五，就得到平均值。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source: Old French meien 'middle', from Latin medianus, not from the English verb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自另一来源：古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus，与英语动词无关。

senses.title: The middle between extremes
senses.definition: a middle point equally distant from two extremes
senses.definitionCN: 与两个极端等距的中间点
senses.example: The golden mean lies between excess and defect.
senses.exampleCN: 中庸之道位于过度与不足之间。
senses.why: The same 'middle' sense serves ethics as well as arithmetic, naming the point that is neither too much nor too little.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「中间」义既用于算术也用于伦理，指既不过多也不过少的那一点。

senses.title: Unkind in manner
senses.definition: unkind, spiteful or deliberately hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 不友善、带恶意或故意伤人的
senses.example: It was mean of him to laugh at her mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他嘲笑她的错误，未免刻薄。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a third source, Old English gemæne 'common, shared', whose sense sank from 'common' to 'inferior' and then to 'petty'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自第三个来源，古英语 gemæne「共同的、共享的」，词义从「共同」降到「低劣」，再降到「小气」。

senses.title: Stingy with money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend or share what one has
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或不愿分享所有
senses.example: He is too mean to buy a second chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他太吝啬，连第二把椅子都不肯买。
senses.why: A person who keeps everything for himself is 'common' in the old sense of ordinary and small, and the word settled into stinginess.
senses.whyCN: 把一切都留给自己的人在旧义上显得「普通而小气」，于是这个词固定为吝啬。

senses.title: Remarkable in the phrase 'no mean'
senses.titleCN: 固定说法中意为「不小的」
senses.definition: not small or easy, used in the fixed phrase no mean feat
senses.definitionCN: 不小、不容易，用于固定说法「不小的成就」
senses.example: Finishing the climb in one day was no mean feat.
senses.exampleCN: 一天之内爬完这段路可不是小事。
senses.why: The phrase works by understatement: it denies the small reading of the adjective in order to praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法用反语：否定形容词「小」的那一面，从而达到称赞。

intro.en: Mean has three separate sources that happen to share one spelling: the verb 'to intend' from Old English mænan, the noun 'average' from Old French meien and Latin medianus, and the adjective 'petty, stingy' from Old English gemæne 'common'.
intro.cn: mean 有三个恰好同形的来源：表示「意图」的动词出自古英语 mænan；表示「平均值」的名词出自古法语 meien 与拉丁 medianus；表示「小气、刻薄」的形容词出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」。

items.en: Mænan meant 'to intend, signify'. Its deeper Germanic origin is not settled; the usual comparison with German meinen is a family resemblance rather than a proved derivation.
items.cn: mænan 意为「意图、意指」。其更早的日耳曼来源无定论；通常把它与德语 meinen 相比，那只是同族相似，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Gemæne meant 'common, shared'. The sense passed from 'common' to 'ordinary, inferior' and then to 'petty, stingy', a downward slide recorded in Middle English.
items.cn: gemæne 意为「共同的、共享的」。词义从「共同」经「普通、低劣」滑向「小气、吝啬」，这一下移在中古英语中已有记录。

items.en: Meien 'middle' entered English in the fourteenth century as the name of the middle value, and it is the source of the average sense.
items.cn: meien「中间」在十四世纪进入英语，指居中的那个数值，是平均值义的来源。

items.en: Medianus 'of the middle' comes from medius 'middle', the same root that gives median, medium and mediate.
items.cn: medianus「中间的」出自 medius「中间」，同一词根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.en: English spelling merged the three histories into one written form, which is why a single entry must keep verb, average and adjective apart.
items.cn: 英语拼写把这三段历史并成一个书写形式，因此同一个词条必须把动词、平均值与形容词分开。

items.en: Exact first citations for each strand are approximate: the verb is Old English, the average noun is fourteenth-century, and the stingy adjective is later Middle English.
items.cn: 三条线索的确切首见书证都只是约数：动词属古英语，平均值名词属十四世纪，吝啬形容词属中古英语后期。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives that are easily mistaken for the same word; group two holds words that share one of the three meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被当成同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是分别与三种含义之一相近的词。

entries.definition: The third-person singular of the verb, and separately a plural noun meaning 'resources'; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数，另有一个表示「资源、手段」的复数名词；都不是那个形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of the verb; the spelling no longer shows the vowel of the base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词；拼写已看不出原形元音。

entries.definition: From the same Latin root as the average sense, but it names the middle item of an ordered set, not the sum divided by the count.
entries.definitionCN: 与平均值义同出拉丁词根，但指按序排列后居中的那一项，而非总和除以个数。

entries.definition: Latin medius as a noun: the middle, or a means between two sides; it has nothing to do with intending.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 medius 的名词形式：中间，或两端之间的媒介；与「意图」无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the sum divided by the count; mean is its technical doublet in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指总和除以个数；在统计中 mean 是它的技术性同义词。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something, close to the 'be a sign' sense of mean.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某事的符号，接近 mean 的「预示」义。

entries.definition: To have a purpose, the plain equivalent of the 'plan' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有目的，是「打算」义的直白对应词。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend or share, the direct synonym of the adjective in its money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或分享，是形容词在钱财义上的直接同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three histories share one spelling: intend, middle, and common-turned-petty.
normal.cn: 三段历史共用一种拼写：意图、中间、由「共同」转来的小气。

normal.en: The verb is irregular in sound but regular in pattern: means, meant, meant, meaning.
normal.cn: 动词读音不规则但形式规律：三单、过去式、过去分词、现在分词依次为 means、meant、meant、meaning。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: mean to do, mean well, the mean value, no mean feat.
normal.cn: 固定说法把义项分开：打算做、出于好意、平均值、不小的成就。

normal.en: The average sense came through French, so it belongs with median and medium rather than with the verb.
normal.cn: 平均值义经法语而来，因此它与 median、medium 同族，而不属于动词那一支。

normal.en: The unkind sense began as 'common', which then meant 'ordinary' and finally 'petty'.
normal.cn: 刻薄义起于「共同的」，再变成「普通的」，最后成了「小气的」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at the one thing a vague sentence was trying to say.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指出一句含混的话真正想说的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales settling exactly level, with equal weights on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平恰好停在水平位置，两边重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a man counting coins twice before he will spend a single one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把硬币数了两遍才肯花掉一枚。

examples.en: A green light means that the road is clear.
examples.cn: 绿灯表示道路畅通。

examples.en: The mean of the class scores rose after the extra lesson.
examples.cn: 加课之后，全班成绩的平均值上升了。

examples.en: It was mean of them to leave her out of the invitation.
examples.cn: 他们把她排除在邀请之外，实在刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词那一支表示「意图、意指」；平均值那一支来自法语里的「中间」；形容词那一支从「共同的」滑到「普通」，再滑到「小气」。三支同形，要按上下文分开。

root: 三条互不同源的线索合成一个拼写：动词出自古英语 mænan「意图、意指」，更早来源无定论；平均值义出自古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus、medius；形容词义出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」，词义下滑为「低劣、小气」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses come from three histories: intending and signifying, the middle value, and the small or petty. The entry keeps them apart so that no sentence is read through the wrong history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项来自三段历史：意图与意指、居中的数值、以及小气刻薄。本词条把它们分开，免得用错历史去读一个句子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand points at what a sentence intends, while a balance beside it rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一句话所意图的东西，旁边的天平恰好水平。

branches.en: SIGNIFY: a word and a red sky both point to what they intend.
branches.cn: 意指：一个词与一片红霞都指向它们所意图的东西。

branches.en: INTEND: purpose is what a person means to do.
branches.cn: 意图：目的就是一个人打算做的事。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE: the average and the golden mean are one position seen numerically and ethically.
branches.cn: 中间：平均值与中庸是同一点在数字与伦理上的两个看法。

branches.en: COMMON TO PETTY: the adjective slid from shared to ordinary to stingy.
branches.cn: 由共同到小气：形容词从「共享」滑到「普通」再到「吝啬」。

branches.en: UNDERSTATEMENT: denying 'small' is a way of saying 'large'.
branches.cn: 反语：否定「小」，正是说「大」。

intro.en: One spelling serves three families, so the affix view must be split: a Germanic verb, a Germanic adjective, and a Latin root for the middle.
intro.cn: 一种拼写服务于三个词族，因此按语素读时必须拆开：一个日耳曼动词、一个日耳曼形容词，以及一个表示「中间」的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The verb family is Germanic, with no Latin kin; the average sense belongs to Latin medius, which also gives median, medium and mediate.
latinIntro.cn: 动词一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族；平均值义属拉丁 medius，同根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.example: The Old English verb is the source of the 'signify' senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词是「意指」诸义的来源。

items.example: The adjective began as 'shared' and ended as 'stingy'.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「共享」开始，最后落到「吝啬」。

items.example: The Latin root supplies the average and middle senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词根提供平均值与中间诸义。

items.example: The derived adjective gives median.
items.exampleCN: 这个派生形容词给出 median。

items.example: I mean the second door.
items.exampleCN: 我指的是第二扇门。

items.structure: mean + -ing (noun suffix, result of an action)
items.example: The meaning is clear.
items.exampleCN: 意思很清楚。

items.meaning: in a petty or stingy way
items.example: He spoke meanly of the offer.
items.exampleCN: 他刻薄地评价那个提议。

items.meaning: the quality of being petty or stingy
items.example: Their meanness surprised the guests.
items.exampleCN: 他们的吝啬让客人吃惊。

latinEntries.structure: medius, media, medium (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: n. 椭圆；椭圆轨道；椭圆形
definition_en: a closed curve where the sum of the distances to two fixed points is constant
core_image: 纸板上按着两颗图钉，套上一圈线，铅笔绷着线画了一整圈，纸上留下两端略尖的闭合图形；星图上行星轨道被画成压扁的圆，太阳偏在一侧焦点上
scene: 天文课上老师把两颗图钉按在纸板上，套上一圈线，用铅笔绷着线画了一整圈。 The pencil traced an ellipse around the two pins.
sceneCN: 这里 ellipse 指「到两个定点的距离之和为常数的闭合曲线」（第 1 个义项：椭圆）；句意是铅笔绕着两颗图钉画出一个椭圆。图中可辨识物件：两颗图钉、线圈、铅笔、闭合图形。

senses.title: The closed oval curve
senses.definition: a closed curve where the sum of the distances to two fixed points is constant
senses.definitionCN: （名词）到两个定点的距离之和为常数的闭合曲线
senses.example: The pencil traced an ellipse around the two pins.
senses.exampleCN: 铅笔绕着两颗图钉画出一个椭圆。
senses.why: Two pins on cardboard with a loop of string held taut by a pencil tip.
senses.whyCN: 纸板上两颗图钉，一圈线被铅笔尖绷得笔直。

senses.title: The shape of an orbit
senses.definition: the oval path followed by a planet or a satellite
senses.definitionCN: （名词）行星或卫星沿行的椭圆形路径
senses.example: Kepler showed that each planet moves on an ellipse with the sun at one focus.
senses.exampleCN: 开普勒证明每颗行星都沿椭圆运行，太阳位于一个焦点上。
senses.why: A star chart with a flattened ring and the sun drawn off to one side.
senses.whyCN: 一张星图上画着压扁的环，太阳偏在一侧。

senses.title: The drawn oval
senses.definition: an oval figure drawn or cut as a shape
senses.definitionCN: （名词）画出或剪出的椭圆形图形
senses.example: The architect cut an ellipse out of the cardboard for the window opening.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师从纸板上剪下一个椭圆，作为窗洞的形状。
senses.why: A cardboard sheet with an oval hole and the cut piece lying beside it.
senses.whyCN: 一张纸板上有个卵形的洞，剪下的那片搁在旁边。

intro.en: Ellipse is Greek elleipsis, a falling short, from elleipein, which joins en- meaning in to leipein meaning to leave; Apollonius used the falling-short idea to name the oval curve.
intro.cn: ellipse 就是希腊语 elleipsis（不足、欠缺），来自 elleipein，它把 en-（在内）与 leipein（留下）结合；阿波罗尼奥斯用「不足」这个想法命名了那条卵形曲线。

items.en: Greek leipein means to leave or leave behind.
items.cn: 希腊语 leipein 意为留下、撇下。

items.en: Adding en- gives elleipein, to fall short in.
items.cn: 加 en- 构成 elleipein，意为在其中有所不足。

items.en: The noun elleipsis names a falling short, applied by Apollonius to the oval curve.
items.cn: 名词 elleipsis 指「不足」，阿波罗尼奥斯用它命名那条卵形曲线。

items.en: Latin took ellipsis for both the omission and the curve.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ellipsis 既指省略，也指那条曲线。

items.en: English split ellipse for the shape and ellipsis for the omission in the 17C.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪把 ellipse 分给图形、ellipsis 分给省略。

items.en: Kepler showed that planets move on an ellipse with the sun at one focus.
items.cn: 开普勒证明行星沿椭圆运行，太阳位于一个焦点上。

note.en: Ellipse and ellipsis sound almost the same and share the Greek root for leaving; ellipse keeps the shape, ellipsis keeps the leaving out of words.
note.cn: ellipse 与 ellipsis 读音几乎一样，共用希腊语「留下」的词根；ellipse 保留了图形，ellipsis 保留了「把词省去」的意思。

examples.cn: 建筑师从纸板上剪下一个椭圆，作为窗洞的形状。

dict_mnemonic.text: ellipse 与 ellipsis 同出希腊语 elleipsis「不足、留下」，词根 leipein＝留下。英语在 17 世纪把两者分家：ellipse 专指「椭圆」，ellipsis 专指「省略；省略号（…）」。形容词 elliptical 两头都管：an elliptical orbit 椭圆轨道，an elliptical remark 省略得让人猜的话。同根还有 eclipse（ec- 向外 ＋ leipein 留下＝光被留下外面＝食）与 ecliptic（黄道，因为食只发生在这条线上）。几何记忆法：两颗图钉 ＋ 一圈线 ＋ 一支铅笔＝椭圆，两钉就是两个焦点 foci，线长不变就是「距离之和为常数」。长轴 major axis、短轴 minor axis、离心率 eccentricity。近义 oval 泛指卵形（不要求两焦点），circle 是离心率为零的特殊椭圆。

root: 希腊语 en-（在内）＋ leipein（留下）→ elleipein → elleipsis（不足）→ ellipse（椭圆）

sensesIntro.en: A circle pressed flat at two points: a taut loop of string around two pins, a flattened ring on a star chart and an oval hole cut in cardboard.
sensesIntro.cn: 被两个点压扁的圆：绕着两颗图钉绷紧的线圈、星图上压扁的环，以及纸板上剪出的卵形洞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pins on cardboard with a loop of string held taut by a pencil tip
core.cn: 核心意象：纸板上两颗图钉，一圈线被铅笔尖绷得笔直

branches.en: A closed curve with two fixed points.
branches.cn: 带两个定点的闭合曲线。

branches.en: The oval path of a planet.
branches.cn: 行星的椭圆形路径。

branches.en: An oval drawn or cut as a shape.
branches.cn: 画出或剪出的卵形图形。

branches.en: Both are the same curve in different use.
branches.cn: 两者是同一条曲线的不同用法。

branches.en: Both name the oval figure itself.
branches.cn: 两者都指卵形图形本身。

intro.en: Ellipse is el- plus leip-; -tical gives elliptical, -is gives ellipsis and ec- gives eclipse and ecliptic.
intro.cn: ellipse 由 el- 加 leip- 组成；-tical 给出 elliptical，-is 给出 ellipsis，ec- 给出 eclipse 与 ecliptic。

latinIntro.en: Greek leipein means to leave; Latin ovum means egg and circulus a little ring, the roots of oval and circle.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 leipein 意为留下；拉丁语 ovum 意为卵，circulus 意为小环，它们是 oval 与 circle 的词根。

definition_zh: 使最小化；把……降到最低；贬低；淡化
definition_en: to reduce something to the smallest possible amount or degree, or to treat it as less important than it really is
core_image: 把一只旋钮一路拧到最左端、直到归零的位置
scene: 外科医生先花一小时规划更小的切口，尽量少出血。 The surgeon spent the first hour planning a smaller incision to minimize blood loss.
sceneCN: 这里 minimize 是「把失血降到最低」（第 4 个义项：把损害、伤害减轻到最小）；句意：外科医生用第一个小时设计更小的切口，以把失血降到最低。场景要点：手术灯下的切口标记、旁边摆着的一袋备用血、医生反复比量的尺子；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.zh: 把出错的可能性降到最低

derivatives.zh: 最小值；最低限度；最小的
极小的；最低限度的
最小化；最小化过程
把事物压到最小的人；求极小值者
极简主义
使最小化（英式拼写）

senses.title: Reach the mathematical minimum
senses.definition: to find or reach the lowest value of a function, quantity, or variable
senses.definitionCN: 求取或达到函数、数量、变量的最低值
senses.example: We minimize the cost function by adjusting both weights at once.
senses.exampleCN: 我们同时调整两个权重，使代价函数取最小值。
senses.why: Latin minimus names the bottom point of a scale. The verb makes an object arrive at that point, so the mathematical sense is the image in its plainest form.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minimus 指刻度的底端。这个动词让对象抵达那个点，因此数学义是这幅意象最朴素的形态。

senses.title: Cost: squeeze the spending down
senses.definition: to keep costs, spending, or prices as low as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把成本、开支或价格保持在尽可能低的水平
senses.example: The airline minimized costs by flying older planes.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司靠飞更旧的飞机把成本压到最低。
senses.why: Cost is a quantity on a dial. Turning that dial to the left end is the budget version of the gesture, and it is the most common business use.
senses.whyCN: 成本是刻度盘上的一个量。把旋钮拧到最左端，就是同一个动作在预算里的版本，也是商业中最常见的用法。

senses.title: Risk: keep the danger small
senses.definition: to reduce the probability or size of a possible harm
senses.definitionCN: 降低某种可能伤害的发生概率或规模
senses.example: Investors diversify their holdings to minimize risk.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者分散持仓，以把风险降到最低。
senses.why: Risk is a probability of loss. Minimizing it moves that probability toward zero, the floor of its own small scale.
senses.whyCN: 风险是损失发生的概率。最小化就是把这个概率推向零，也就是它自己那一小段刻度的底端。

senses.title: Damage: leave as little harm as possible
senses.definition: to limit the harm done to people, property, or the environment
senses.definitionCN: 限制对人、财产或环境造成的伤害
senses.example: The spill was contained to minimize damage to the river.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏被控制住，以把对河流的损害减到最小。
senses.why: Damage is what remains after an accident. Minimizing it means shrinking the remainder, not preventing the accident itself.
senses.whyCN: 损害是事故之后留下的东西。最小化是把这个剩余量缩小，而不是阻止事故本身。

senses.title: Error and delay: shrink the unwanted amount
senses.titleCN: 错误与延误：把不需要的量缩小
senses.definition: to make errors, delays, or other unwanted quantities as small as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把错误、延误或其他不想要的量做到尽可能小
senses.example: Every figure was checked twice to minimize the chance of error.
senses.exampleCN: 每个数字都核对了两遍，以把出错的可能性降到最低。
senses.why: An error is an unwanted quantity on a scale that one would rather see at zero. The same verb now measures what should not be there.
senses.whyCN: 错误是一把尺子上不希望出现的量，人们宁愿它停在零。这个动词于是用来衡量“本不该存在的东西”。

senses.title: Computing: shrink a window to a corner
senses.titleCN: 计算机：把窗口缩到角落
senses.definition: to reduce a window on a screen to a small bar or icon
senses.definitionCN: 把屏幕上的窗口缩成一条小栏或一个图标
senses.example: Click the minus sign to minimize the window.
senses.exampleCN: 点击减号即可把窗口最小化。
senses.why: A window has a size scale whose floor is the smallest allowed bar. The command drives it to that floor, making the metaphor visible as a button.
senses.whyCN: 窗口有一个尺寸刻度，它的底端就是允许的最小条栏。这个命令把窗口推到那层底端，让比喻变成了一个可见的按钮。

senses.title: Downplay a person's role
senses.definition: to make someone's contribution or importance seem smaller than it is
senses.definitionCN: 使某人的贡献或重要性显得比实际更小
senses.example: The report minimizes the role of local volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告贬低了当地志愿者的作用。
senses.why: The scale has moved from things to reputation: a person's role is described as if it occupied a smaller notch than it really does.
senses.whyCN: 尺子从实物移到了名声：一个人的作用被说成只占一个比实际更小的刻度。

senses.title: Soften the seriousness of something
senses.definition: to speak of a problem or danger as less serious than it is
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或危险说得没有实际那么严重
senses.example: Officials minimized the seriousness of the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们淡化了这次泄漏的严重性。
senses.why: Here the quantity being reduced is not the harm but the reported size of the harm; the words shrink the picture while the thing stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里被缩小的不是伤害本身，而是伤害被报告出来的大小；话把画面缩小了，而事情本身没有变。

senses.title: Engineering: cut a design down to essentials
senses.titleCN: 工程：把设计削减到本质
senses.definition: to reduce the number of parts, steps, or features in a design to the smallest workable set
senses.definitionCN: 把设计中的零件、步骤或功能削减到可工作的最小集合
senses.example: The redesign minimizes moving parts and therefore wear.
senses.exampleCN: 重新设计把活动部件减到最少，因此也减少了磨损。
senses.why: Fewer parts means less on the scale. Minimizing here is not about one number but about removing everything that is not needed.
senses.whyCN: 零件更少，意味着刻度上的东西更少。这里的最小化不是压一个数字，而是删掉一切不必要的东西。

intro.en: Minimize is an English coinage of 1802 from minimum + -ize. Its Latin base and the later 'belittle' sense are both documented; dates are those given by standard etymological references.
intro.cn: minimize 是 1802 年由 minimum 加 -ize 构成的英语自造词。它的拉丁词基以及后来“贬低”的义项都有记载；年代采用通行词源资料的说法。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'to reduce to a minimum, make as little as possible'. It is an English formation from minimum + -ize, first attested in Bentham.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 1802 年，意为“减到最低、使尽可能小”。它是由 minimum 加 -ize 构成的英语自造词，最早可考的使用者是边沁。

items.en: Minimum entered English meaning 'the smallest portion into which matter is divisible', a sense now obsolete; it came from Latin minimum, the neuter of minimus 'smallest'.
items.cn: minimum 于 17 世纪 60 年代进入英语，意为“物质可分割的最小部分”，这一义项今已废弃；它来自拉丁语 minimum，即 minimus“最小的”的中性形式。

items.en: Latin minimus is the superlative of minor 'smaller', and minor belongs to the same family as minus and minuere 'to lessen'. The whole set describes one end of a scale.
items.cn: 拉丁语 minimus 是 minor“更小的”的最高级，而 minor 与 minus、minuere“减少”同属一个词族。整组词描述的是同一把尺子的一端。

items.en: The family goes back to PIE *mei- (2) 'small', the root also behind diminish, minute, minuscule, minister and minutia.
items.cn: 这个词族可追溯到原始印欧语 *mei-（第二支）“小”，该词根也是 diminish、minute、minuscule、minister、minutia 的来源。

items.en: The sense 'to depreciate, treat slightingly' is recorded. This is the branch that lets minimize mean 'belittle' as well as 'reduce', and it explains why the word can sound evasive.
items.cn: “贬低、轻视地对待”这一义项于 1875 年有记录。正是这一支让 minimize 既能表示“减少”，也能表示“贬低”，也解释了它为何有时听起来像在回避。

items.en: British spelling is minimise. Minimization, minimizer, minimal and minimalism fill out the family. Maximize and minimize are a matched pair, both recorded in 1802 and both used by Bentham.
items.cn: 英式拼写为 minimise。minimization、minimizer、minimal、minimalism 补足了词族。maximize 与 minimize 是一对配套词，都记录于 1802 年，都出自边沁。

note.en: The first group separates the noun, the adjective, the British spelling and the rare short noun. The second group compares minimize with plain reduce, with lessen, with rhetorical downplay, and with its exact opposite, maximize.
note.cn: 第一组区分名词、形容词、英式拼写和一个罕见的短名词；第二组把 minimize 与普通的 reduce、与 lessen、与修辞上的 downplay，以及它的正对面 maximize 作比较。

entries.definition: the smallest amount or degree possible. It is the noun that minimize was built from, not a synonym of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小数量或程度。它是构成 minimize 的名词词基，而不是这个动词的同义词。

entries.definition: very small in amount or degree. It describes a state, while minimize names the act of bringing that state about.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或程度极小的。它描述一种状态，而 minimize 命名把这种状态造成出来的动作。

entries.definition: the British spelling of minimize, with -ise instead of -ize. It is the same word, not a different meaning.
entries.definitionCN: minimize 的英式拼写，用 -ise 代替 -ize。它是同一个词，不是另一个词义。

entries.definition: a tiny amount, or a note of very short duration. It shares the 'small' root but is not a form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的量，或时值很短的音符。它共享“小”的词根，却不是这个动词的词形。

entries.definition: to make something smaller in size or amount. It names the movement, not the floor: a reduced price need not be the lowest possible price.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物在尺寸或数量上变小。它命名移动，而不命名底端：降价并不等于降到可能的最低价格。

entries.definition: to make something smaller in degree or intensity, often a feeling or an effect. It is more literary and more limited than minimize.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事物在程度或强度上变小，常指感受或效果。它比 minimize 更书面，适用范围也更窄。

entries.definition: to make something seem less important than it is. It targets the description, while minimize can target either the thing or the description.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事物显得没有实际那么重要。它针对的是描述，而 minimize 既可针对事物，也可针对描述。

entries.definition: to make as great as possible. It is the exact opposite pole: one verb turns the dial to the left, the other to the right.
entries.definitionCN: 使尽可能大。它正是对立的那一端：一个动词把旋钮向左拧，另一个向右拧。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: minimum + -ize, the Latin superlative minimus, the *mei- 'small' family, and the matched pair minimize / maximize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：minimum 加 -ize、拉丁最高级 minimus、*mei-“小”词族，以及成对的 minimize／maximize。

normal.en: Minimum is the floor of a scale and -ize means 'to make'. Minimize is simply 'to make minimum'.
normal.cn: minimum 是刻度的底端，-ize 意为“使……”。minimize 就是“使达到最小”。

normal.en: Minimus is the Latin superlative of minor 'smaller'; the same root gives minimum, minor, minus and diminish.
normal.cn: minimus 是拉丁语 minor“更小的”的最高级；同一词根还给出 minimum、minor、minus、diminish。

normal.en: Minimize and maximize were both recorded in 1802, both in Bentham: one drives to the floor of the scale, the other to the ceiling.
normal.cn: minimize 与 maximize 都记录于 1802 年，都出自边沁：一个把刻度推到低端，一个推到顶端。

normal.en: In business writing minimize collocates with risk, cost, damage, loss and disruption — unwanted quantities that one wants near zero.
normal.cn: 在商业写作里，minimize 常与 risk、cost、damage、loss、disruption 搭配——都是人们希望接近零的不想要的量。

normal.en: In computing, minimize is the button that shrinks a window to a bar; the smallest allowed bar is the floor of that scale.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，minimize 是把窗口缩成一条栏的按钮；允许的最小条栏就是那把尺子的底端。

abstract.en: Picture a dial with a hard stop at the left end. You can turn it down to the stop and no further; that stop is what minimum means.
abstract.cn: 想象一只左端有硬止点的旋钮。你能把它拧到止点，再也不能多拧一格；那个止点就是 minimum 的含义。

abstract.en: A minimum is a floor, not a direction: minimizing tells you where to stop, not how much effort it takes to get there.
abstract.cn: 最小值是地板，不是方向：minimize 告诉你该停在哪里，却没说你得花多大力气走到那里。

abstract.en: The same verb can shrink a thing or shrink its description. Shrinking the description is what makes minimize sound like an excuse.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词既能缩小事物，也能缩小对事物的描述。缩小描述，正是 minimize 听起来像借口的缘故。

examples.en: Keep the lid on the pan to minimize evaporation.
examples.cn: 盖上锅盖，把蒸发减到最少。

examples.en: The company moved its servers abroad to minimize tax.
examples.cn: 这家公司把服务器迁到国外，以把税负压到最低。

examples.en: She minimized her own part in the rescue.
examples.cn: 她把自己在救援中的作用说得很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: “迷你麦子”——把麦子磨得越来越小，最后只剩手心里一小撮 → minimize 最小化、降到最低

root: 由 minimum“最小量”加 -ize“使……”构成，minimum 又来自拉丁语 minimus“最小的”，核心是“把某物拧到刻度的最左端”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of minimize, all from one gesture: a dial is turned to the far left until it reaches the floor, whether the scale measures a function, a cost, a risk, a window, or a person's reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: minimize 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把旋钮一路拧到最左端，直到触底——无论这把尺子量的是函数、成本、风险、窗口，还是一个人的名声。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned to the far left until it stops at the bottom of its scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旋钮被拧到最左端，停在刻度的底端。

branches.en: NUMBERS: a function has a lowest value, and minimizing moves the result down to that value.
branches.cn: 数值：函数有一个最低值，最小化就是把结果压到那个值上。

branches.en: COST AND ENGINEERING: money, risk and moving parts are quantities to be cut down to the floor.
branches.cn: 成本与工程：金钱、风险与活动部件都是要被削到底端的量。

branches.en: HARM: damage and the chance of error are remainders to be shrunk so that as little as possible is left.
branches.cn: 伤害：损害与出错概率都是要被缩小的剩余量，好让最后剩下的尽可能少。

branches.en: INTERFACE: the window shrinks to the smallest allowed bar, its own floor.
branches.cn: 界面：窗口缩到允许的最小条栏，也就是它自己的底端。

branches.en: RHETORIC: a person's role or a danger is made to look smaller than it is, so the scale now measures appearance.
branches.cn: 修辞：一个人的作用或一桩危险被说得比实际小，于是这把尺子量的是“看起来的大小”。

intro.en: Minimize is a complete noun plus a living suffix: minimum + -ize. The same Latin superlative supplies a large family of words about smallness and reduction.
intro.cn: minimize 是一个完整名词加一个活后缀：minimum 加 -ize。同一个拉丁最高级还供应了一大群关于“小”与“减少”的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin minimus 'smallest' is the superlative of minor 'smaller', itself formed from the *mei- family. Minimum is the neuter form used as a noun; minus is a related neuter form meaning 'less'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minimus“最小的”是 minor“更小的”的最高级，而 minor 本身出自 *mei- 词族。minimum 是作名词用的中性形式；minus 是表示“更少”的相关中性形式。

items.meaning: to make as small as possible
items.meaningCN: 使尽可能小；最小化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The plan minimizes the number of transfers.
items.exampleCN: 这个方案把换乘次数减到最少。

items.meaningCN: 最小量；最低限度（-um 为中性最高级词尾）
items.example: The machine needs a minimum of two litres of oil.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器至少需要两升油。

items.meaningCN: 极小的；最低限度的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The storm caused minimal damage.
items.exampleCN: 这场风暴造成的损害极小。

items.meaning: the process of reducing something to the least possible
items.meaningCN: 最小化；最小化过程（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Waste minimization saved the plant a fortune.
items.exampleCN: 把浪费最小化为工厂省下一大笔钱。

items.meaning: one who seeks the minimum, or a device that reduces something
items.meaningCN: 求最小值者；把事物压到最小的人或装置（-er 表示行为者）
items.example: As a minimizer, he packs only what fits in one bag.
items.exampleCN: 作为一个凡事求最少的人，他只带一个包能装下的东西。

items.example: The guide advises households to minimise water use.
items.exampleCN: 这份指南建议家庭把用水减到最少。

items.meaning: a tiny amount; a note of short duration
items.meaningCN: 极小的量；短音符（来自拉丁语 minimus）
items.example: The recipe calls for a minim of salt.
items.exampleCN: 这份食谱只要一丁点儿盐。

items.meaningCN: 减去；负号；不利因素（拉丁语 minus，minor 的中性形式）
items.example: Ten minus four is six.
items.exampleCN: 十减四等于六。

items.meaningCN: 减少；削弱（di- 离开 + minuere 减少）
items.example: The noise diminished as the train moved away.
items.exampleCN: 火车开远后，噪声渐渐变小。

items.meaningCN: 极小的（作形容词，来自拉丁语 minutus“小的”）
items.example: A minute crack appeared in the glass.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃上出现了一道极细的裂缝。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 更小的；较少的；较年幼的

latinEntries.structure: neuter of minimus, used as a noun
latinEntries.meaningCN: 最小者；最小量（minimus 的中性形式作名词）

definition_zh: 美术（尤指绘画、雕塑、建筑等）；高雅艺术；精湛技艺
definition_en: art valued for beauty and expression rather than practical use, especially painting, sculpture and architecture
core_image: 一件不拿来用的东西被放在台座上，只为让人看
scene: 谈判桌上，老练的中间人先让对方把底线说出来，再慢慢回应。 The mediator practised the fine art of letting the other side speak first.
sceneCN: 这里 fine art 用于固定说法「the fine art of...」，指「需要高超技巧与分寸的技艺」（第 8 个义项：某种精细的处事本领）；句意为调停者运用「先让对方开口」这门精细手艺。

pos.zh: 美术；高雅艺术（通常不可数）；the fine art of... 指精湛技艺

derivatives.zh: fine art + -s（复数）→ 各门美术；从「类别」转到「多门学科集合」
fine art + -ist（从业者）→ 美术家；从「领域」转到「人」
fine artist + -s（复数）→ 美术家们；仅数量变化

senses.title: Art valued for beauty, not use
senses.titleCN: 以美与表达为目的而非实用的艺术
senses.definition: art made chiefly to be beautiful or expressive rather than useful
senses.definitionCN: 主要为美或表达而创作、而非为实用的艺术
senses.example: The museum separates fine art from design.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把美术与设计分开。
senses.why: Fine here carries its old sense of 'of the highest quality', and art carries 'skill'; together they name work whose end is aesthetic rather than practical.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 fine 保留旧义「最高品质」，art 保留「技艺」；合起来命名以审美而非实用为目的的作品。

senses.title: The fine arts as a group
senses.definition: the group of disciplines traditionally including painting, sculpture and architecture
senses.definitionCN: 传统上包括绘画、雕塑与建筑的一组学科
senses.example: The academy teaches the fine arts as separate departments.
senses.exampleCN: 学院把各门美术分成独立系科教授。
senses.why: The plural turns the category into a list: each medium becomes a discipline, and the phrase names them together.
senses.whyCN: 复数把类别变成清单：每种媒介成为一门学科，短语把它们合称。

senses.title: A particular work of fine art
senses.definition: one work belonging to the fine arts
senses.definitionCN: 属于美术门类的一件作品
senses.example: The auction offered a fine-art piece by a living sculptor.
senses.exampleCN: 拍卖会推出一件在世雕塑家的美术作品。
senses.why: Category names can be used for members, especially in attributive form, so a single object can be marked as belonging to fine art.
senses.whyCN: 类别名称可用于成员，尤其在定语形式中，因此单件物品可以被标记为属于美术。

senses.title: The border with craft
senses.definition: the category defined against craft and applied art
senses.definitionCN: 通过与工艺、应用艺术对照而界定的类别
senses.example: The show blurs the line between fine art and craft.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览模糊了美术与工艺的界线。
senses.why: A category needs an outside: fine art is what claims beauty before function, while craft is judged by use and technique.
senses.whyCN: 类别需要一个外部：美术声称美先于功能，而工艺按用途与技术来评判。

senses.title: The market and collecting
senses.definition: the commercial field of dealers, auctions and collectors in fine art
senses.definitionCN: 画商、拍卖与收藏者构成的美术商业领域
senses.example: Fine art sales outperformed the wider market.
senses.exampleCN: 美术品销售表现优于整体市场。
senses.why: Unique objects need a market of their own, so the category name becomes a trade label for authenticated originals.
senses.whyCN: 独一无二的物件需要自己的市场，因此类别名称成为经认证原作的交易标签。

senses.title: Photography's contested place
senses.definition: the debated inclusion of photography within fine art
senses.definitionCN: 摄影是否属于美术的争论
senses.example: Photography fought for a place in fine art for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 摄影为进入美术之列争取了一个世纪。
senses.why: A reproductive medium challenged the category's claim to unique handmade beauty, so the phrase became the prize in that argument.
senses.whyCN: 可复制的媒介挑战了该类别对独一无二手作之美的声称，因此这个短语成了争论的奖品。

senses.title: Training and the academy
senses.definition: the academic training and institutions devoted to fine art
senses.definitionCN: 专攻美术的学院训练与机构
senses.example: She studied fine art before turning to set design.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学美术，后来转向舞台设计。
senses.why: Academies turned the category into a curriculum, so the phrase also names the degree and the studio training.
senses.whyCN: 学院把类别变成课程，因此这个短语也命名学位与工作室训练。

senses.title: The 'fine art of' doing something
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase the fine art of, a skill requiring delicacy and judgement
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法 the fine art of 中，指需要细腻与判断力的技艺
senses.example: The mediator practised the fine art of letting the other side speak first.
senses.exampleCN: 调停者运用「先让对方开口」这门精细手艺。
senses.why: The phrase borrows the prestige of fine art for ordinary skills: anything done with delicacy can be dressed as an art, and 'fine' adds the note of refinement.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法把美术的声望借给日常技能：任何做得细腻的事都能被包装成一门艺术，而 fine 加上「精细」的意味。

intro.en: Fine art is an eighteenth-century English phrase translating French beaux-arts; fine goes back through Old French to Latin finis, and art to Latin ars. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fine art 是 18 世纪英语短语，译自法语 beaux-arts；fine 经古法语上溯拉丁 finis，art 上溯拉丁 ars。年代均为约数。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary'; Old French fin developed the sense 'perfected, of the highest quality', generally explained by the notion of the end or peak of a scale.
items.cn: finis 意为「终点、边界」；古法语 fin 发展出「精炼的、最高品质的」之义，通常用「量程的终点或顶点」来解释。

items.en: Ars, artis meant practical skill or craft, and by the Renaissance it also named the liberal and visual arts.
items.cn: ars、artis 意为实用技艺或手艺，到文艺复兴也用来指自由艺术与视觉艺术。

items.en: French beaux-arts, literally 'beautiful arts', named the arts of beauty in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
items.cn: 法语 beaux-arts 字面为「美的艺术」，在 17 与 18 世纪指以美为目标的艺术。

items.en: English fine art is recorded around 1760 as a translation of beaux-arts, at first in the singular as a category name.
items.cn: 英语 fine art 约 1760 年有记录，是 beaux-arts 的翻译，最初以单数作类别名。

items.en: Nineteenth-century art schools and exhibitions separated fine art from applied art and craft, fixing the modern contrast.
items.cn: 19 世纪的艺术学校与展览把美术与应用艺术、工艺分开，确立了现代对照。

items.en: Twentieth-century auction houses and galleries made fine art a market category for unique, authenticated works.
items.cn: 20 世纪的拍卖行与画廊使美术成为独一无二、经认证作品的交易类别。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from forms that look almost identical; group two separates it from categories that overlap but judge by a different standard.
note.cn: 第一组把该短语与几乎同形的形式分开；第二组把它与有重叠、但按不同标准评判的类别分开。

entries.definition: The several disciplines taken together, especially in a faculty or degree title; fine art can name the category as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 各门学科合称，尤用于学院或学位名称；fine art 可指整体类别。

entries.definition: The French phrase from which fine art translates; in English it often appears in institutional names.
entries.definitionCN: fine art 所译的法语短语；在英语中常出现在机构名称里。

entries.definition: On its own fine means excellent, thin or delicate; only in the phrase does it mark the category of beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时意为优良、纤细或精细；只有在这个短语里才标记美的类别。

entries.definition: A practitioner of fine art, as opposed to a commercial or applied artist.
entries.definitionCN: 美术从业者，相对于商业或应用艺术家。

entries.definition: Art considered serious and culturally elevated; the label is social, while fine art is categorical.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为严肃而有文化高度的艺术；这个标签是社会性的，而 fine art 是类别性的。

entries.definition: Art addressed to the eye, including photography and design; fine art decides by beauty rather than by sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以眼睛为对象的艺术，包括摄影与设计；fine art 按美而非按感官划分。

entries.definition: Art made to serve a practical function; it is the usual opposite of fine art.
entries.definitionCN: 为实用功能而作的艺术；是 fine art 的常用反义类别。

entries.definition: Making by hand with trained skill, often useful; fine art claims aesthetic value beyond technique.
entries.definitionCN: 以训练有素的技艺手工制作，常具实用性；fine art 声称技法之外还有审美价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fine (of the highest quality) + art: art at the top of the scale.
normal.cn: fine（最高品质）+ art：处在价值序列顶端的艺术。

normal.en: The phrase translates French beaux-arts, literally 'beautiful arts'.
normal.cn: 这个短语译自法语 beaux-arts，字面是「美的艺术」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: fine art gallery, fine art photography, the fine art market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：美术画廊、艺术摄影、美术市场。

normal.en: The family runs fine, fine arts, fine artist and beaux-arts.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 fine、fine arts、fine artist 与 beaux-arts。

normal.en: The idiom the fine art of... borrows the prestige of the category for ordinary delicacy.
normal.cn: 固定说法 the fine art of... 把类别的声望借给日常的精细手艺。

abstract.en: Picture an object put on a pedestal precisely because it is useless.
abstract.cn: 想象一件正因为它没用而被放上台座的物品。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn between a bowl and a painting, and both sides arguing.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画在碗与画之间的线，两边都在争论。

abstract.en: Picture a certificate that says the object may be looked at, not used.
abstract.cn: 想象一张证书，写明这件东西可供观看，不可使用。

examples.en: Fine art training begins with drawing, whatever medium follows.
examples.cn: 美术训练从素描开始，之后才分媒介。

examples.en: The gallery's fine art collection is shown beside its design archive.
examples.cn: 画廊的美术收藏与设计档案并置展出。

examples.en: He admired the fine art with which she ended the meeting.
examples.cn: 他佩服她结束会议时那份精细的分寸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fine（精细的）+ art（艺术）」——做得精细的艺术 → 美术

root: fine 经古法语 fin「精炼的、最高品质的」上溯拉丁 finis「终点、边界」；art 来自拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺」。fine art 约 1760 年译自法语 beaux-arts。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the category to its disciplines, one work, the border with craft, the market, photography's argument, academic training and finally the idiom of delicate skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从类别转到各门学科、单件作品、与工艺的界线、市场、摄影之争、学院训练，最后落到精细技艺的固定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object that is not for use is placed on a pedestal so that it can be looked at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件不供使用的物品被放上台座，只为让人观看。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY AND ITS DISCIPLINES: one name, then a list of media.
branches.cn: 类别及其学科：一个名称，然后是一串媒介。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the category applied to a single piece.
branches.cn: 物件：类别被用于单件作品。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the category exists by separating itself from craft.
branches.cn: 边界：类别通过与工艺分离而存在。

branches.en: MARKET AND ARGUMENT: authenticated originals, and the medium that fought for entry.
branches.cn: 市场与争论：经认证的原作，以及为进入而抗争的媒介。

branches.en: TRAINING AND PHRASE: the academy's curriculum, then the idiom of delicate skill.
branches.cn: 训练与说法：学院的课程，然后是精细技艺的固定表达。

intro.en: Fine art is a two-word phrase, not a derivational family; its first element is a French adjective of quality and its second a Latin noun of skill.
intro.cn: fine art 是两词短语，而非派生词族；第一个成分是表示品质的法语形容词，第二个是表示技艺的拉丁名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis and ars are the deep sources, but the phrase itself was formed in French and English, not in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 finis 与 ars 是深层来源，但短语本身是在法语与英语中形成的，不在拉丁语中。

items.structure: Old French fin, from Latin finis (end, limit)
items.example: Fine here means refined, not thin.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 fine 指精炼，而非纤细。

items.example: Art supplies the second element.
items.exampleCN: art 提供第二个成分。

items.meaning: art of beauty rather than use
items.meaningCN: 以美而非实用为目的的艺术
items.example: Fine art was separated from craft.
items.exampleCN: 美术与工艺被分开。

items.example: The faculty lists the fine arts separately.
items.exampleCN: 学院把各门美术分列。

items.example: The fine artist works in bronze.
items.exampleCN: 这位美术家做青铜。

items.example: The suffix names the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名人。

items.example: The school kept its French name.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校保留了法语名称。

items.example: The frame is an artistic choice.
items.exampleCN: 画框是一种艺术选择。

definition_zh: 军事战役；为达成明确目标而在一定战区连续实施的一系列作战行动
definition_en: a connected series of military operations, fought over a period of time in one theatre, that pursues a defined objective
core_image: 指挥所地图上，一支粗箭头从滩头伸向内陆，旁边钉着一叠日历，每一页都画着一次推进
scene: 指挥所的地图上，一支粗箭头从滩头一路伸向内陆，旁边钉着一叠日历，每一页都画着一次推进。 The general planned a military campaign that would end before the winter rains.
sceneCN: 这里 military campaign 指「为达成明确目标而在战区连续实施的一系列作战行动」（第 1 个义项：把多次交战串成有起止、有目标的整体）；句意为将军筹划了一场要在冬雨之前结束的军事战役。图中可辨识物件：指挥所地图、粗箭头、滩头标记、钉着的日历。

pos.zh: 军事战役；有明确目标的一连串作战行动（复合名词；复数作 military campaigns）

collocations.phrase: a military campaign against the rebels

derivatives.zh: 军事的；军队（拉丁 militaris「士兵的」，由 miles「士兵」加 -aris 而来；miles 更深来源不确定）
以军事手段；在军事上（military 加 -ly，由形容词转为方式副词）
军国主义（military 加 -ism，指把军事优先当作治国原则的意识形态）
军事化（military 加 -ize，转为「使某物带上军事性质」）
战役；运动（法语 campagne < 意大利 campagna「开阔田野」< 拉丁 campus「田野」，由「野外」转为「野外作战」，再转为「有组织的运动」）
运动参与者；竞选者（campaign 加 -er，指持续投入一场运动的人）
校园；田野（拉丁 campus「田野」，与 campaign 同源，后转指学校或机构的场地）

senses.title: A connected series of operations
senses.titleCN: 为达成目标而连成一片的系列作战
senses.definition: several battles and supporting actions linked by one aim, one commander and one span of time
senses.definitionCN: 由同一目标、同一指挥官与同一段时间串起来的多次交战与支援行动
senses.example: The spring military campaign opened with two river crossings.
senses.exampleCN: 春季军事战役以两次渡河开始。
senses.why: Campaign came from 'open country', and armies that fought there called the whole season of manoeuvres by the name of the ground.
senses.whyCN: campaign 出自「开阔田野」，在那种地形作战的军队就把整季的机动都按这片地面来命名。

senses.title: A single operation with a defined objective
senses.titleCN: 一次有明确目标的作战行动
senses.definition: one operation whose success is judged by taking a city, clearing a route or destroying a force
senses.definitionCN: 以攻占城市、打通路线或消灭一支力量为成败标准的一次行动
senses.example: The military campaign had one objective: to cut the railway before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这场军事战役只有一个目标：在冬季到来之前切断铁路。
senses.why: An aim narrows the series into a single measurable task, and ordinary usage still calls that task a campaign.
senses.whyCN: 目标把系列行动收窄为一项可衡量的任务，而日常用法仍把这项任务称为 campaign。

senses.title: A theatre-level joint operation
senses.definition: the coordinated work of land, sea and air forces inside one theatre under a single plan
senses.definitionCN: 在同一战区、同一方案下由陆海空力量协同实施的行动
senses.example: The joint military campaign required the navy to hold the strait while the air force blinded the radar.
senses.exampleCN: 这场联合军事战役要求海军守住海峡，同时空军使雷达失效。
senses.why: Modern commands fight one theatre as a whole, so the word covers the joint product rather than any single service's part.
senses.whyCN: 现代指挥把整个战区当作一体来打，因此这个词涵盖联合作战的产物，而非某一军种的那一部分。

senses.title: A battle in the history books
senses.definition: a named episode in military history, dated and mapped as a unit in a textbook or gallery
senses.definitionCN: 军事史中一个有名称的片段，在教科书或展馆里被当作有年代、有地图的单位
senses.example: The museum's second hall is devoted to the military campaign of that autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的第二个展厅专门陈列那个秋天的军事战役。
senses.why: Once it is over and dated, a campaign becomes a chapter, and the word shifts from action to historical object.
senses.whyCN: 一旦结束并被系上年代，一场战役就变成一章，词义也从行动转为历史对象。

senses.title: The planning stage of a campaign
senses.definition: the staff work of aims, phases, logistics and timing before the first unit moves
senses.definitionCN: 在第一支部队出动之前，对目标、阶段、后勤与时序所作的参谋工作
senses.example: The military campaign was won in the planning room long before the first shot.
senses.exampleCN: 这场军事战役早在第一枪打响之前就已在作战室里赢下了。
senses.why: Planning is the campaign's brain, so the same word names the paper phase as well as the fighting.
senses.whyCN: 筹划是战役的大脑，因此同一个词既指纸面阶段，也指实际交战。

senses.title: A long expeditionary war
senses.definition: a distant, prolonged operation sustained by supply lines and reinforcements rather than one decisive battle
senses.definitionCN: 靠补给线与增援而非一场决战来维持的远距离持久行动
senses.example: A military campaign across the desert consumed more fuel than the fighting consumed ammunition.
senses.exampleCN: 横越沙漠的军事战役消耗的燃料比交战消耗的弹药还多。
senses.why: Distance and duration make the campaign a way of life for an army, and the word grows to cover that whole stretch.
senses.whyCN: 距离与时间使这场行动成为军队的一种生活方式，词义也随之覆盖整段过程。

senses.title: An air campaign
senses.definition: a sustained bombing or interdiction effort run as a campaign in its own right
senses.definitionCN: 作为一场独立战役来实施的持续轰炸或阻断行动
senses.example: The military campaign in the air struck bridges for six weeks before the ground advance.
senses.exampleCN: 空中军事战役在地面推进之前连续六周打击桥梁。
senses.why: Air power can now conduct its own connected series, so it borrows the word once reserved for armies.
senses.whyCN: 空中力量如今能独自实施连成一片的系列行动，于是借用了原属陆军的这个词。

senses.title: A figurative organized push
senses.titleCN: 比喻性的有组织攻坚行动
senses.definition: a journalistic use for a sustained drive by an institution to win a market, a vote or a reform
senses.definitionCN: 新闻用法，指机构为赢得市场、选票或改革而持续发起的行动
senses.example: The bank's military campaign against fraud used the vocabulary of fronts and reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行打击欺诈的军事战役借用了前线与预备队的词汇。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the shape of linked actions under one aim, which is what any sustained institutional push has.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「同一目标下连成一片的行动」这一结构，而任何持续的组织攻坚都具有这种结构。

intro.en: The adjective comes from a Latin word for a soldier, while the noun comes from a Latin word for open field by way of Italian and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 形容词来自拉丁语中表示士兵的词，名词则经意大利语与法语来自拉丁语中表示开阔田野的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Miles meant 'soldier'; its deeper origin is source uncertain, and no earlier root is reliably attested.
items.cn: miles 意为「士兵」；其更深来源属来源不确定，没有可靠书证的更早词根。

items.en: Militaris, built with the adjectival ending -aris, meant 'of a soldier' and is the direct source of English military.
items.cn: militaris 由形容词词尾 -aris 构成，意为「士兵的」，是英语 military 的直接来源。

items.en: Campus meant an open field or plain, the flat ground where armies could deploy.
items.cn: campus 指开阔的田野或平原，即军队可以展开的平地。

items.en: Campagna named open country, and Italian soldiers applied it to a season of operations in the field.
items.cn: campagna 指开阔乡野，意大利军人把它用于一季的野外作战。

items.en: French borrowed campagne and passed it to English, where the military sense and the political sense grew side by side.
items.cn: 法语借入 campagne 再传入英语，军事义与政治运动义在此并行生长。

items.en: English joined the adjective to the noun to name a connected operation; the exact first use is source uncertain and the dates are approximate.
items.cn: 英语把形容词与名词连起来指连成一片的作战；确切的最早书证属来源不确定，年代为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the two halves of the phrase from related words that share their roots but not their job; group two holds military actions of different scale.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语的两半与同根但职能不同的词分开；第二组是规模不同的军事行动。

entries.definition: Of soldiers or armed forces; it describes the instrument, while the phrase names the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 指士兵或武装部队的；它描述的是工具，而这个短语命名的是行动。

entries.definition: The operation itself or an organized public drive; the phrase pins it to warfare.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动本身，也指有组织的公众运动；这个短语把它固定在军事上。

entries.definition: From Latin campus 'field', now the grounds of a school or company; it shares a root but not a war.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 campus「田野」，现指学校或公司的场地；同根但与战争无关。

entries.tag: same field stock a place to stay
entries.definition: A place where troops or travellers pitch tents; it is related through the field image, not the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 指部队或旅人搭帐篷的地方；它通过「田野」意象相连，并非作战行动。

entries.definition: A single planned action within a campaign; several operations make the campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 指一场战役中的单次计划行动；若干次行动才构成战役。

entries.definition: A journey undertaken for a purpose, often military; it stresses distance rather than the connected series.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某一目的进行的远行，常为军事性质；它强调距离，而非系列行动。

entries.definition: The attacking part of a campaign; a campaign may include offensives and pauses.
entries.definitionCN: 指战役中的进攻部分；一场战役可以包含进攻与停顿。

entries.definition: One engagement between forces; a campaign contains several battles and the marches between them.
entries.definitionCN: 指两支力量的一次交战；一场战役包含若干次战斗以及其间的行军。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Miles 'soldier' plus -aris gives militaris, the adjective behind military.
normal.cn: miles「士兵」加 -aris 得 militaris，即 military 背后的形容词。

normal.en: Campus 'field' gives campagna 'open country', and a campaign is a season of fighting in the open.
normal.cn: campus「田野」得 campagna「开阔乡野」，而战役就是一季在野外的作战。

normal.en: The campaign family runs campus, campagna, campagne, campaign, campaigner, campaigning.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 campus、campagna、campagne、campaign、campaigner、campaigning。

normal.en: Collocations show the stages: launch a military campaign, conduct a military campaign, military campaign planning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示阶段：发动军事战役、实施军事战役、军事战役筹划。

normal.en: The phrase has two levels: a campaign is a series, a battle is one item in it.
normal.cn: 这个短语有两个层级：战役是系列，战斗是其中一项。

abstract.en: Picture one long arrow drawn across a map with many small dates pinned along it.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着一支长箭头，沿线钉着许多小日期。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer's field turned into a grid of tents and supply dumps.
abstract.cn: 想象一片农夫的田野被改成由帐篷与补给堆组成的网格。

abstract.en: Picture a relay race in which each runner must hand over before the next can start.
abstract.cn: 想象一场接力赛，每一棒都必须交接之后下一棒才能起跑。

examples.en: The military campaign stalled when the rains turned the roads into mud.
examples.cn: 雨水把道路变成泥浆之后，这场军事战役停滞了。

examples.en: Historians describe the military campaign as a series of missed chances.
examples.cn: 历史学家把这场军事战役描述为一连串错失的机会。

examples.en: Supply trucks, not tanks, decided the outcome of the military campaign.
examples.cn: 决定这场军事战役结局的是补给卡车，而不是坦克。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「military（士兵的）+ campaign（田野里打仗）」——把许多场战斗连成一季的野外行动 → 军事战役

root: 军事：拉丁 militaris「士兵的」< miles「士兵」，miles 更深来源属来源不确定。战役：法语 campagne < 意大利 campagna「开阔田野」< 拉丁 campus「田野」；「战役」义由「在野外作战」引申，与 camp 同源。两半不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one connected operation: it is a series, then a single task, then a joint theatre, a dated chapter, a planning room, a long expedition, an air effort, and finally any organized institutional push.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一场连贯行动展开：它先是系列，再是一项任务，继而成为联合战区、有年代的一章、作战室、长期远征、空中行动，最后是任何有组织的机构攻坚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one long arrow crosses a map, and every date pinned along it belongs to the same push.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支长箭头横穿地图，沿箭头钉着的每一个日期都属于同一次推进。

branches.en: SERIES AND TASK: the connected whole and the one measurable aim are the same word at two zoom levels.
branches.cn: 系列与任务：连成的整体与那一项可衡量的目标，是同一个词在两个缩放层级上的样子。

branches.en: THEATRE AND CHAPTER: a joint operation in the field later hardens into a dated historical unit.
branches.cn: 战区与章节：野外的联合作战后来凝固为有年代的历史单位。

branches.en: BRAIN AND DISTANCE: the planning room and the long expedition are the start and the stretch of one campaign.
branches.cn: 大脑与距离：作战室与长期远征，是一场战役的起点与长度。

branches.en: AIR ARM: bombing can run its own connected series and so borrows the army's word.
branches.cn: 空中一翼：轰炸能独自构成系列行动，于是借用了陆军的词。

branches.en: METAPHORICAL PUSH: any institution that links actions under one aim repeats the shape.
branches.cn: 比喻攻坚：任何把行动串在同一目标下的机构，都在重演这一结构。

intro.en: The phrase is two borrowed halves: a Latin adjective of soldiers and a Latin field noun that reached English through Italian and French.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个借来的部分组成：一个拉丁语的士兵形容词，和一个经意大利语与法语进入英语的拉丁语田野名词。

latinIntro.en: Miles supplies the soldier half through militaris, and campus supplies the field half through campagna and campagne.
latinIntro.cn: miles 经 militaris 提供「士兵」一半，campus 经 campagna 与 campagne 提供「田野」一半。

items.example: The noun is the human unit behind the whole adjective family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个形容词词族背后的人之单位。

items.example: The suffix turns a soldier into an adjective of soldiers.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「士兵」变成「士兵的」形容词。

items.example: The adjective keeps the human reference of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留了名词所指的人。

items.example: English uses the word for both the institution and its adjective.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个词既用于军队机构，也用作其形容词。

items.example: The flat ground is the place where a deployed army stands.
items.exampleCN: 这片平地就是展开的军队所站之处。

items.example: Italian shifts the field word toward the countryside around a town.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语把这个田野词转向城镇周边的乡野。

items.meaning: a season of operations; an organized drive
items.meaningCN: 一季作战；有组织的运动
items.example: The word moves from ground to season to organized effort.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从地面转到季节，再转到有组织的努力。

items.example: The suffix yields campaigner from campaign.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 campaign 造出 campaigner。

items.example: The suffix yields campaigning, the running of a campaign.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出 campaigning，即开展一场运动的过程。

items.example: The suffix yields militarism, a doctrine of military priority.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀造出 militarism，即军事优先的主义。

definition_zh: 生物；有机体；生物体；（社会或组织的）有机整体
definition_en: an individual living thing, or a whole whose parts work together like those of a living body
core_image: 一个由许多器官协同工作的完整生命体，每个部件都为整体服务
scene: 一只小小的生物体内，细胞数量可能比这座城市的人口还多。 A single organism can contain more cells than there are people in the city.
sceneCN: 这里 organism 指「生物」（第 1 个义项：独立存活的个体生命）；句意：一个生物体内的细胞数可能超过这座城市的人口。图中可辨识物件：示意的细胞群、器官剖面、放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 生物；有机体；生物体；（比喻）有机整体、组织体

derivatives.zh: 有机的；生物的；有机农业的
生物个体的；个体层面的
有机整体的；整体论的
组织；机构；安排
器官；机构；风琴
细胞器

senses.title: An Individual Living Thing
senses.definition: a single living thing, such as an animal, plant or bacterium
senses.definitionCN: 单个活物，如动物、植物或细菌
senses.example: A single organism can contain more cells than there are people in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 一个生物体内的细胞数可能超过这座城市的人口。
senses.why: Greek organon meant 'tool, instrument'. An organism is a body whose parts work as instruments for the whole, which is why the word stresses organized cooperation rather than mere life.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 意为「工具、器具」；organism 是各部件作为整体之工具而协同工作的身体，因此这个词强调有组织的协作，而不只是「活着」。

senses.title: Microscopic Life
senses.titleCN: 微生物：肉眼难见的个体
senses.definition: a microscopic living thing, especially a bacterium or fungus
senses.definitionCN: 微小的活物，尤指细菌或真菌
senses.example: The water contained several harmful organisms.
senses.exampleCN: 水中含有几种有害微生物。
senses.why: In hygiene and medicine the word usually points to things too small to see. The size is not part of the definition, but the context supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 在卫生与医学语境里，这个词通常指小到看不见的东西；大小并不属于定义，而是由语境补上的。

senses.title: A Social Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：社会或组织的比喻
senses.definition: a society or organization treated as a body whose parts depend on one another
senses.definitionCN: 被看作相互依存之身体的社会或组织
senses.example: Some nineteenth-century writers called society a living organism.
senses.exampleCN: 一些十九世纪的作家把社会称为活的有机体。
senses.why: The metaphor claims that institutions are not assembled machines but growing bodies. It has been used both to justify reform and to argue that parts cannot be replaced at will.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻主张制度不是拼装的机器，而是生长出来的身体；它既被用来支持改革，也被用来论证各部分不能随意替换。

senses.title: Engineered Life
senses.titleCN: 改造过的生物：转基因个体
senses.definition: a living thing whose genetic material has been deliberately altered
senses.definitionCN: 遗传物质被人为改动的活物
senses.example: Regulations cover any genetically modified organism sold as food.
senses.exampleCN: 法规涵盖任何作为食品出售的转基因生物。
senses.why: Modern biotechnology made the word a legal category. The organism is still an individual living thing; only its genes have been edited, which is why the modifier carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 现代生物技术把这个词变成法律类别；该生物仍是独立活物，只是基因被编辑过，因此分量落在修饰语上。

senses.title: Model Organism
senses.titleCN: 模式生物：用于研究的代表
senses.definition: a species studied in the laboratory to understand general biological processes
senses.definitionCN: 在实验室中研究、以理解一般生物过程的物种
senses.example: The fruit fly became the model organism for genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇成了遗传学的模式生物。
senses.why: Research needs a stand-in that is easy to keep and well understood. The word marks the individual, while the phrase marks its representative role.
senses.whyCN: 研究需要一个易饲养、已被充分理解的替身；这个词标出的是个体，而短语标出的是它的代表角色。

senses.title: An Ecological Unit
senses.titleCN: 生态个体：生态学中的计数单位
senses.definition: an individual counted as a unit in an ecological study
senses.definitionCN: 生态研究中作为一个单位来计数的个体
senses.example: The survey counted every organism larger than a millimetre.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查统计了每一个大于一毫米的生物个体。
senses.why: Ecology counts individuals to estimate populations. Here the word is almost a unit of measurement, defined by the size cut-off the researcher chooses.
senses.whyCN: 生态学通过数个体来估计种群；此时这个词几乎是一个计量单位，其边界由研究者选定的尺寸下限决定。

senses.title: An Organized Whole
senses.titleCN: 有机整体：哲学意义上的整体
senses.definition: a whole whose parts are mutually dependent and cannot be understood alone
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相互依赖、不能孤立理解的整体
senses.example: For the philosopher, the mind is an organism, not a machine.
senses.exampleCN: 在这位哲学家看来，心灵是有机整体，而不是机器。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word against mechanism. If parts only make sense in the whole, explanation must begin with the whole, not with the smallest piece.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用这个词来反对机械论：如果部件只有在整体中才有意义，解释就必须从整体开始，而不是从最小零件开始。

senses.title: A Working Body
senses.titleCN: 运作中的组织体：机构如身体
senses.definition: an organization understood through the cooperation of its parts
senses.definitionCN: 通过各部分协作来理解的机构
senses.example: The department behaves like an organism with its own metabolism.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门像一个有自己的代谢方式的有机体那样运作。
senses.why: Management writing borrows the biological image to talk about flow, feedback and adaptation. The claim is that removing one part changes the health of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 管理写作借生物学意象来谈流动、反馈与适应；其主张是：拿掉一个部件会改变其余部分的健康。

intro.en: Organism is a modern formation on Greek organon 'tool, instrument, organ', from ergon 'work'. It was coined in the nineteenth century; the exact coiner and first date are uncertain.
intro.cn: organism 是建立在希腊 organon「工具、器具、器官」之上的近代构词，而 organon 出自 ergon「工作」。该词于十九世纪被造出；确切的造词者与首见年代不确定。

items.en: Ergon meant 'work, deed'. Its Indo-European root also gives English work and the Greek adjective energetikos, source of energy.
items.cn: ergon 意为「工作、行动」，其印欧词根也给出英语 work，以及希腊形容词 energetikos——energy 的来源。

items.en: Organon meant 'a tool or instrument', and by extension an organ of the body, since an organ is the body's instrument for a task. Aristotle's logical works were called the Organon, the tool of reasoning.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，引申指身体器官，因为器官就是身体完成某项任务的工具。亚里士多德的逻辑著作被称为 Organon，即推理的工具。

items.en: Latin organum kept the senses of instrument and, later, musical instrument and body organ. English organ and organize descend from this line.
items.cn: 拉丁 organum 保留「器具」义，后来又指乐器与身体器官；英语 organ 与 organize 都出自这条线索。

items.en: Organism was formed in the nineteenth century to name a living body as an organized whole. The exact coiner is uncertain; the word spread with biology and with the philosophy of organized wholes.
items.cn: organism 于十九世纪被造出，用来指作为有组织整体的活体。确切的造词者不确定；该词随生物学以及「有组织整体」的哲学而传播开来。

items.en: Social thinkers soon applied organism to societies and institutions. The metaphor was attractive because it explained interdependence, but it was also criticized for making change seem like mere growth.
items.cn: 社会思想家很快把 organism 用于社会与机构。这个比喻之所以有吸引力，是因为它能解释相互依存；但它也因让变革显得只是「生长」而受到批评。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective relatives and from organization. The second holds near-synonyms that name life at different scales.
note.cn: 第一组区分该名词与其形容词亲属以及 organization；第二组是不同尺度上指称生命的近义词。

entries.definition: Means 'of living things' or 'grown without chemicals'. It describes a quality, while organism names the living individual.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「生物的」或「不用化学方式种植的」；它描述性质，而 organism 命名的是活的个体。

entries.definition: A structured group such as a company, or the act of arranging. It shares the organ root but names arrangement, not life.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指公司一类有结构的人群，或安排的动作；它同出 organ 词根，但命名的是安排，而不是生命。

entries.definition: A body part with a specific function, or a musical instrument. It is the instrument that the organism as a whole uses.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指有特定功能的身体部件，或指乐器；它是整个 organism 所使用的「工具」。

entries.definition: A living being, especially an animal. It is warmer and less technical than organism.
entries.definitionCN: 活物，尤指动物；比 organism 更有温度，技术性更弱。

entries.definition: A living entity, or existence itself. It is broader and vaguer, often used where organism would sound clinical.
entries.definitionCN: 活的存在者，或存在本身；更宽泛、更模糊，在 organism 显得过于临床的地方常用它。

entries.definition: A microscopic living thing. It is narrower than organism, which covers elephants as well as bacteria.
entries.definitionCN: 微小的活物；比 organism 狭窄，因为后者同样包括大象与细菌。

entries.definition: Any kind of living thing, often used when imagining life elsewhere. It stresses kind rather than individual.
entries.definitionCN: 任何种类的活物，常用于设想别处的生命；强调种类而非个体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: organon 'tool' + -ism: a body whose organs are tools for the whole.
normal.cn: organon「工具」+ -ism：器官作为整体工具的身体。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organic, organism, organismal, organismic, organize, organization, organelle.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organic、organism、organismal、organismic、organize、organization、organelle。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: living organism, model organism, single-celled organism, genetically modified organism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：生物、模式生物、单细胞生物、转基因生物。

normal.en: organism is the living thing; organization is the arranged group.
normal.cn: organism 是活的东西，organization 是安排成的群体。

normal.en: organic describes a quality; organism names the individual.
normal.cn: organic 描述性质，organism 命名个体。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every tool has its place and every worker serves the same finished object.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊，每件工具都有位置，每个工人服务于同一件成品。

abstract.en: Picture a city that repairs its own roads without anyone giving the order.
abstract.cn: 想象一座自己修补道路、无需谁下命令的城市。

abstract.en: Picture a watch that grows new wheels instead of replacing them.
abstract.cn: 想象一只表会自己长出新的齿轮，而不是更换齿轮。

examples.en: No organism can survive without water for long.
examples.cn: 没有生物能在缺水的情况下长期存活。

examples.en: The pond supports thousands of microscopic organisms.
examples.cn: 这个池塘养育着数以千计的微小生物。

examples.en: The model organism is chosen because its genome is small.
examples.cn: 选择该模式生物，是因为它的基因组很小。

dict_mnemonic.text: organ（器官）+ ism（体系、状态）→ 由器官协同构成的整体 → 生物、有机体

root: 希腊 ergon「工作」→ organon「工具、器官」→ 拉丁 organum → 英语 organ → 十九世纪加 -ism 构成 organism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all concern an organized living whole: an individual, a microbe, a society, an engineered plant or animal, a laboratory model, an ecological unit, a philosophical whole and a working institution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都涉及有组织的活的整体：个体、微生物、社会、被改造的动植物、实验室模型、生态单位、哲学整体与运作中的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many organs working as one body, each part serving the whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多器官作为一个身体协同工作，每个部件都为整体服务。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL UNIT: from a whale to a bacterium, one living thing counted as one.
branches.cn: 个体单位：从鲸到细菌，一个活物算作一个。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE MAJORITY: hygiene and medicine use the word for life too small to see.
branches.cn: 看不见的多数：卫生与医学用这个词指小到看不见的生命。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL METAPHOR: societies and departments are described as bodies whose parts depend on each other.
branches.cn: 社会比喻：社会与部门被描述为部件相互依存的身体。

branches.en: LIFE UNDER DESIGN: engineered organisms and model organisms exist because humans chose and altered them.
branches.cn: 被设计过的生命：转基因生物与模式生物之所以存在，是因为人选择并改动了它们。

branches.en: THE PHILOSOPHICAL WHOLE: against mechanism, the whole explains the parts rather than the reverse.
branches.cn: 哲学整体：与机械论相对，整体解释部件，而不是反过来。

intro.en: Organism is a Greek-derived root with the English suffix -ism: an instrument-root, a suffix of system or state, and later a biological noun.
intro.cn: organism 是希腊来源的词根加英语后缀 -ism：表示器具的词根、表示体系或状态的后缀，后来成为生物学名词。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon reached Latin as organum and produced organ, organic, organism, organize, organization and organelle. The root ergon also underlies energy.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 以拉丁 organum 进入拉丁语，衍生 organ、organic、organism、organize、organization、organelle；词根 ergon 也支撑 energy。

items.example: The organism responds to light within seconds.
items.exampleCN: 该生物在数秒内就对光作出反应。

items.meaning: of living things; grown without chemicals
items.meaningCN: 生物的；不用化学方式种植的
items.example: Organic matter in the soil feeds the crop.
items.exampleCN: 土壤中的有机物滋养作物。

items.meaning: at the level of the individual organism
items.example: Organismal responses differ from cellular ones.
items.exampleCN: 个体层面的反应不同于细胞层面的反应。

items.meaning: treating the whole as an organized body
items.example: Organismic biology studies wholes, not only parts.
items.exampleCN: 有机体生物学研究整体，而不只是部件。

items.meaning: a body part with a task
items.meaningCN: 承担某项任务的身体部件
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.meaning: a small structure inside a cell
items.example: The chloroplast is an organelle.
items.exampleCN: 叶绿体是一种细胞器。

items.meaning: to arrange parts into a working whole
items.meaningCN: 把部件安排成可运作的整体
items.example: She organized the files by year.
items.exampleCN: 她按年份整理了文件。

items.meaning: an arranged group or the act of arranging
items.meaningCN: 安排成的群体或安排的行为
items.example: The organization has forty staff.
items.exampleCN: 该组织有四十名员工。

latinEntries.structure: Greek ergon (work); root also in Latin energia

definition_zh: 杂交；杂交育种；分子杂交；轨道杂化
definition_en: the process of producing hybrids, or the technique of combining complementary strands or orbitals
core_image: 两支不同颜色的线被捻成一股，接头处能看出两种颜色
scene: 实验台上两个亲缘很近的植物被人工授粉。记录员写道： Hybridization produced seeds that germinated faster than either parent.
sceneCN: 这里指「杂交过程」（第 1 个义项：让两个不同物种或品种产生后代的过程）；句意为杂交产生的种子比两个亲本都发芽更快。

pos.zh: 杂交；杂交育种；分子杂交；杂化（不可数，复数 hybridizations 指多次过程）

forms.label: 分词形容词（正在杂交的）

derivatives.zh: 使杂交；杂交
杂种；杂交后代 / 杂交的
杂交性；混合性
混合性；杂合性
杂交瘤

senses.title: The process of crossing
senses.definition: the process by which individuals of different species or varieties produce offspring
senses.definitionCN: 不同物种或品种的个体产生后代的过程
senses.example: Hybridization produced seeds that germinated faster than either parent.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交产生的种子比两个亲本都发芽更快。
senses.why: The suffix -ization names a process, so the word looks at the crossing as an event rather than at the offspring.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ization 命名过程，因此这个词把杂交看作事件，而不是看作后代。

senses.title: Hybridization breeding
senses.definition: the deliberate crossing of selected parents to produce improved varieties
senses.definitionCN: 有意让选配的亲本杂交以产生改良品种
senses.example: Hybridization gave the farm a wheat that ripens earlier.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交育种为农场带来了一个更早成熟的麦种。
senses.why: Agriculture turns the natural process into a planned method, repeated until a stable variety appears.
senses.whyCN: 农业把自然过程变成有计划的方法，重复进行直到稳定品种出现。

senses.title: Molecular hybridization
senses.definition: the pairing of complementary nucleic acid strands from different sources
senses.definitionCN: 来自不同来源的互补核酸链配对
senses.example: DNA hybridization showed that the two samples shared a sequence.
senses.exampleCN: 脱氧核糖核酸杂交显示两个样本共享一段序列。
senses.why: The word is borrowed for molecules because two complementary strands also 'cross' and pair into one double structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被借用于分子，因为两条互补链也会「交叉」并配对成一个双链结构。

senses.title: In situ hybridization
senses.definition: a technique that detects a specific sequence inside intact cells or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 在完整细胞或组织内检测特定序列的技术
senses.example: In situ hybridization located the gene within the tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 原位杂交在组织内定位了该基因。
senses.why: The method keeps the sample in place, so the pairing of probe and target is read exactly where it happens.
senses.whyCN: 这种方法让样本保持原位，因此探针与靶标的配对就在发生处被读出。

senses.title: Somatic cell hybridization
senses.definition: the fusion of two cells from different sources into one hybrid cell
senses.definitionCN: 把不同来源的两个细胞融合成一个杂交细胞
senses.example: Somatic hybridization joined the two cell lines in the dish.
senses.exampleCN: 体细胞杂交在培养皿中把两个细胞系合在一起。
senses.why: Here the 'cross' is between whole cells rather than organisms, and the result is a single fused cell.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「交叉」发生在整个细胞之间而非生物体之间，结果是一个融合细胞。

senses.title: Orbital hybridization
senses.definition: the mixing of atomic orbitals into new equivalent orbitals
senses.definitionCN: 原子轨道混合成新的等价轨道
senses.example: Orbital hybridization explains the shape of the methane molecule.
senses.exampleCN: 轨道杂化解释了甲烷分子的形状。
senses.why: Chemistry borrows the word for the mixing of orbitals, where distinct shapes combine into new ones.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用这个词指轨道的混合，不同的形状组合成新的形状。

senses.title: Interspecific hybridization
senses.definition: crossing between different species, which may transfer genes between them
senses.definitionCN: 不同物种之间的杂交，可能在它们之间转移基因
senses.example: Interspecific hybridization can introduce new alleles into a species.
senses.exampleCN: 种间杂交可以把新等位基因引入一个物种。
senses.why: In evolution the process is a channel for gene flow, and the word names the channel rather than the product.
senses.whyCN: 在进化中，这一过程是基因流动的通道，这个词命名通道而非产物。

senses.title: Cultural hybridization
senses.definition: the blending of cultural forms into something new
senses.definitionCN: 文化形式融合成新事物的过程
senses.example: Cultural hybridization shaped the city's food and music.
senses.exampleCN: 文化混合塑造了这座城市的饮食与音乐。
senses.why: The biological process becomes a metaphor for traditions meeting and producing a new form.
senses.whyCN: 生物过程变成隐喻，指传统相遇并产生新的形式。

intro.en: Hybridization is an English derivative: hybrid plus -ization. Hybrid comes from Latin hybrida. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hybridization 是英语派生词：hybrid 加 -ization。hybrid 来自拉丁 hybrida。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hybrida named the offspring of two kinds; English hybrid descends from it and supplies the base of hybridization.
items.cn: hybrida 指两个种类的后代；英语 hybrid 承自它，并提供 hybridization 的词基。

items.en: The suffix -ization came through French from Latin -izatio, a noun of process built on -izare.
items.cn: 后缀 -ization 经法语来自拉丁 -izatio，是建立在 -izare 之上的过程名词。

items.en: Hybridization spread in the nineteenth century with scientific breeding and the new study of heredity.
items.cn: hybridization 在 19 世纪随科学育种与新的遗传研究而传播。

items.en: The twentieth century added molecular hybridization, once complementary nucleic acid strands could be paired in the lab.
items.cn: 20 世纪增添了分子杂交义，当时互补核酸链已能在实验室中配对。

items.en: Orbital hybridization became a standard term in chemistry after the development of valence theory.
items.cn: 价键理论发展之后，轨道杂化成为化学的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first use of hybridization in each technical field is dated only approximately, and the origin of Latin hybrida remains disputed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：hybridization 在各专业领域的最早使用只有大致年代；拉丁 hybrida 的来源仍有争议。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same hybrid family; group two holds other terms for crossing or combining.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hybrid 词族的形式；第二组是表示杂交或组合的其他术语。

entries.definition: To carry out a cross; hybridization is the process noun built from that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施杂交；hybridization 是由该动词构成的过程名词。

entries.definition: The offspring or the mixed thing itself; hybridization names the making of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指后代或混合事物本身；hybridization 命名其制造过程。

entries.definition: The condition of being hybrid; it is a state, not a process or technique.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为杂交体的状况；是状态，不是过程或技术。

entries.definition: The quality of mixed origin, common in cultural theory; it does not name a laboratory method.
entries.definitionCN: 指混合来源的性质，常见于文化理论；不命名实验室方法。

entries.definition: Deliberate breeding across breeds or varieties; it is close to hybridization but usually applied to farm stock.
entries.definitionCN: 指跨品种或品系的有意繁育；接近 hybridization，但多用于畜禽。

entries.definition: The act of crossing two individuals; it is the plain word, while hybridization is the technical process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指让两个个体杂交的行为；是朴素说法，而 hybridization 是专业过程名词。

entries.definition: The movement of genes from one species into another through repeated crossing; it names the genetic result.
entries.definitionCN: 指基因通过反复杂交从一个物种流入另一个物种；命名遗传结果。

entries.definition: The reshuffling of genes during reproduction; it happens inside a species and is not a cross between species.
entries.definitionCN: 指繁殖过程中基因的重组；发生在物种内部，不是物种间的杂交。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: hybrid + -ization: the process of making a hybrid.
normal.cn: hybrid + -ization：制造杂交后代的过程。

normal.en: The family runs hybrid, hybridize, hybridization, hybridism, hybridity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hybrid、hybridize、hybridization、hybridism、hybridity。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: plant hybridization, DNA hybridization, orbital hybridization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：植物杂交、脱氧核糖核酸杂交、轨道杂化。

normal.en: The suffix -ization always points to a process, not a product.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ization 总是指向过程，而非产物。

normal.en: In the lab, hybridization pairs complementary strands; in the field, it pairs parents.
normal.cn: 在实验室里，杂交让互补链配对；在田间，它让亲本配对。

abstract.en: Picture two colored threads twisted into one cord.
abstract.cn: 想象两根不同颜色的线被捻成一股绳。

abstract.en: Picture two recipes merged into one dish served at a single table.
abstract.cn: 想象两份菜谱合成一道菜，端上同一张桌子。

abstract.en: Picture two tunes played at once until a third melody emerges.
abstract.cn: 想象两支曲子同时演奏，直到浮现出第三段旋律。

examples.en: Hybridization between the two species produced fertile offspring.
examples.cn: 两个物种之间的杂交产生了可育后代。

examples.en: The lab uses hybridization to compare gene sequences.
examples.cn: 实验室用杂交来比较基因序列。

examples.en: Orbital hybridization explains why the bonds are equal.
examples.cn: 轨道杂化解释了为什么这些键是等长的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「海布里代泽申」——把两种血脉接在一起的那道工序 → 杂交

root: hybrid（拉丁 hybrida「不同种类的后代」）+ -ization（拉丁 -izatio，表示过程）；hybrida 的更深来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: two sources are crossed, and the process is then named in farming, molecular biology, cytology, chemistry, evolution and culture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个过程展开：两个来源被交叉，这个过程再在农业、分子生物学、细胞学、化学、进化与文化中获得名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two differently colored threads twisted into one cord.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根不同颜色的线被捻成一股绳。

branches.en: ORGANISMS AND SPECIES: the basic crossing, and the same crossing between distinct species.
branches.cn: 生物体与物种：基本杂交，以及不同物种之间的同一杂交。

branches.en: BREEDING: the process becomes a planned agricultural method.
branches.cn: 育种：这个过程成为有计划的农业方法。

branches.en: MOLECULES: complementary strands pair, and the pairing can be read inside intact tissue.
branches.cn: 分子：互补链配对，而且这种配对可在完整组织内被读出。

branches.en: CELLS: whole cells fuse into one hybrid cell.
branches.cn: 细胞：整个细胞融合成一个杂交细胞。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY AND CULTURE: orbitals mix, and traditions blend.
branches.cn: 化学与文化：轨道混合，传统融合。

intro.en: Hybridization is hybrid plus the process suffix -ization; the base is Latin, the suffix came through French, and the word is a standard technical formation.
intro.cn: hybridization 是 hybrid 加过程后缀 -ization；词基为拉丁来源，后缀经法语而来，整体是标准的技术构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin hybrida gives the base hybrid, and Latin -izatio (through French -isation) gives the suffix; the deeper origin of hybrida is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 hybrida 给出词基 hybrid，拉丁 -izatio（经法语 -isation）给出后缀；hybrida 的更深来源有争议。

items.example: The hybrid is the product of the process.
items.exampleCN: hybrid 是这一过程的产物。

items.example: Hybridize is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: hybridize 是这一名词背后的动词。

items.example: The suffix marks a process, not a result.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记过程，而非结果。

items.example: The plants hybridize easily.
items.exampleCN: 这些植物容易杂交。

items.example: Hybridization can transfer useful genes.
items.exampleCN: 杂交可以转移有用的基因。

items.example: Hybridism appears where two ranges meet.
items.exampleCN: 两个分布区相接处会出现杂交状态。

items.example: Hybridity describes cultural mixing.
items.exampleCN: hybridity 描述文化混合。

items.meaningCN: 产生抗体的融合细胞系
items.example: Hybridoma technology relies on cell fusion.
items.exampleCN: 杂交瘤技术依赖细胞融合。

definition_zh: 湿地；常年或季节性积水、土壤饱和的土地
definition_en: land that is saturated or covered by water for at least part of the year, supporting water-adapted plants
core_image: 芦苇立在浅水里，水面映着天光，水下的泥是黑的，边上就是城镇的排水口
scene: 芦苇立在浅水中，水面映着天光，这片湿地正过滤城镇的径流。 Reeds stood in standing water across the wetland that filters the town's runoff.
sceneCN: 这里 wetland 指「常年或季节性积水、土壤饱和的土地」（第 1 个义项：湿地）；句意为芦苇立在浅水里，这片湿地正过滤城镇的径流。图中可辨识物件：芦苇、浅水、黑色泥底、排水口、水面倒影。

collocations.zh: 拉姆萨尔湿地（国际重要湿地）

derivatives.zh: 湿的；弄湿
潮湿
湿地恢复

senses.title: Land saturated or covered by water
senses.titleCN: 积水或土壤饱和的土地
senses.definition: ground where water stands at or near the surface for long enough each year to shape the soil and the plants
senses.definitionCN: 水每年在表面或近表面停留足够久、从而塑造土壤与植物的地面
senses.example: Reeds stood in standing water across the wetland that filters the town's runoff.
senses.exampleCN: 芦苇立在浅水里，这片湿地正过滤城镇的径流。
senses.why: wet plus land names ground by its water condition, the same way woodland is named by trees.
senses.whyCN: wet 加 land 按水分条件给土地命名，正如 woodland 按树命名。

senses.title: The legal Ramsar definition
senses.titleCN: 拉姆萨尔公约的法律定义
senses.definition: the treaty definition covering marshes, fens, bogs, peatlands and shallow water, natural or artificial, permanent or temporary
senses.definitionCN: 公约定义，涵盖沼泽、矿质沼泽、泥炭沼泽与浅水，天然或人工、永久或暂时
senses.example: The treaty counts a seasonal salt pan as a wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 公约把季节性盐沼也算作湿地。
senses.why: a treaty needed one broad definition, so the word expanded from wet ground to a list of habitat types.
senses.whyCN: 条约需要一个宽泛定义，于是这个词从「湿的地」扩展为一串生境类型。

senses.title: Marsh, swamp, bog and fen types
senses.titleCN: 沼泽、木本沼泽、泥炭沼与矿质沼泽
senses.definition: the main wetland classes, separated by water chemistry, peat depth and whether trees or reeds dominate
senses.definitionCN: 主要湿地类别，按水化学、泥炭厚度与乔木或芦苇占优来区分
senses.example: A fen is fed by groundwater, while a bog is fed only by rain.
senses.exampleCN: 矿质沼泽由地下水补给，泥炭沼只靠雨水补给。
senses.why: one general word needed subdivisions, and each subtype carries its own water source and chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 一个总称需要细分，而每个亚型都有自己的水源与化学。

senses.title: Wetland functions and services
senses.titleCN: 湿地的功能与生态服务
