senses.why: Greek methodos already meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry'. Science did not invent the word; it inherited the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 methodos 本就意为“科学探究、探究的方法”。科学没有发明这个词，它继承的是最古老的义项。

senses.title: Teaching and acting methods
senses.titleCN: 教学法与表演体系：一门手艺的路
senses.definition: a named system of practice in teaching or in the arts, such as the direct method or method acting
senses.definitionCN: 教学或艺术中以人名或特征命名的实践体系，如直接教学法、方法派表演
senses.example: Method acting asks the performer to draw on real memories.
senses.exampleCN: 方法派表演要求演员调动真实的记忆。
senses.why: A system with a name becomes a school. Method here is a path that a whole profession agrees to walk together.
senses.whyCN: 一套有名字的体系会变成一派。这里的 method 是一整门行业同意一起走的那条路。

senses.title: Old medical sense
senses.titleCN: 医学旧义：系统化的治疗方案
senses.definition: in early use, the regular, systematic treatment of disease
senses.definitionCN: 在早期用法中，指对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗
senses.example: The medieval physician spoke of a method for fevers, not a single remedy.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的医生讲的是治疗热病的一套方法，而不是某一味药。
senses.why: The first English sense, in the early 15th century, was 'regular, systematic treatment of disease'. The word entered through medicine before it belonged to everything else.
senses.whyCN: 英语中的第一个义项是 15 世纪初的“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”。这个词先通过医学进来，然后才属于一切别的事物。

senses.title: Method in programming
senses.titleCN: 编程中的方法：对象身上的函数
senses.definition: in object-oriented programming, a function or procedure attached to an object or class
senses.definitionCN: 在面向对象编程中，附着于对象或类上的函数或过程
senses.example: The method returns a new list instead of changing the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法返回一个新列表，而不修改旧列表。
senses.why: The metaphor survives in code: a method is still a fixed route the object knows how to take when it is called.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻在代码里活了下来：方法仍是对象被调用时知道该怎么走的一条固定路线。

senses.title: A method of inquiry
senses.titleCN: 探究之路：哲学意义上的方法
senses.definition: in philosophy, the deliberate path of doubt or reasoning by which a conclusion is reached
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，为抵达结论而有意采取的怀疑或推理之路
senses.example: Descartes began with a method of doubt that would leave only certainty standing.
senses.exampleCN: 笛卡尔从一种怀疑的方法开始，只为留下确定的东西。
senses.why: Methodos was literally a following after something. Philosophy turns that pursuit into a rule for how to pursue anything at all.
senses.whyCN: methodos 字面上就是“跟在某物之后追”。哲学把这趟追寻变成一条规则，规定该怎样追寻任何东西。

senses.title: Method in one's madness
senses.definition: in the phrase 'there is method in one's madness', used when apparently foolish behaviour turns out to have a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 「there is method in one's madness」 中，指看似荒唐的行为其实自有目的
senses.example: He shuffles the cards for ten minutes, but there is method in his madness.
senses.exampleCN: 他把牌洗了十分钟，看似荒唐，其实自有章法。
senses.why: Shakespeare's phrase 'though this be madness, yet there is method in it' (Hamlet) gave English a fixed way to say that a path is hidden inside chaos.
senses.whyCN: 莎士比亚的句子“though this be madness, yet there is method in it”（《哈姆雷特》）给了英语一个固定说法：混乱里藏着一条路。

intro.en: Method is Greek: meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road, way'. Latin borrowed it as methodus and passed it to French and English. It has no connection with medical, despite the shared -met- shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: method 是希腊词：meta“追寻”加 hodos“路、道”。拉丁语把它借作 methodus，再传给法语和英语。尽管有共同的 -met- 外形，它与 medical 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'regular, systematic treatment of disease', through Latin methodus 'way of teaching or going' and Greek methodos.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 15 世纪初，意为“对疾病的规律化、系统化治疗”，经拉丁语 methodus“教学或行走之道”与希腊语 methodos 而来。

items.en: Greek methodos meant 'scientific inquiry, method of inquiry, investigation', and originally 'pursuit, a following after'.
items.cn: 希腊语 methodos 意为“科学探究、探究的方法、调查”，原义为“追寻、跟随其后”。

items.en: The word joins meta 'in pursuit or quest of' and hodos 'a way, path, track, road', also 'a journey'. Hodos is of uncertain origin; Beekes suggests PIE *sod- 'course', and it is traditionally linked to Slavic words for 'course'.
items.cn: 这个词由 meta“追寻、求索”与 hodos“路、路径、轨道、道路”（也指“旅程”）组合而成。hodos 的来源不确定；Beekes 提出原始印欧语 *sod-“行程”，传统上也把它与斯拉夫语表示“行程”的词联系起来。

items.en: The sense widened to 'any way of doing anything' in the 1580s, to 'orderliness, regularity' in the 1610s, and to 'a system or complete set of rules' in the 1680s.
items.cn: 词义在 16 世纪 80 年代扩展到“做任何事的方式”，17 世纪 10 年代扩展到“有条理、有规律”，17 世纪 80 年代扩展到“体系或完整的一套规则”。

items.en: The phrase method acting is recorded in reference to the theory associated with the Russian director Konstantin Stanislavski.
items.cn: method acting 这一说法有记录，指与俄国导演康斯坦丁·斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基相关的理论。

items.en: Medical goes back to Latin medicus 'physician', with no Greek element. Meta- in method is the Greek preposition 'in pursuit of', not the modern prefix meaning 'beyond' or 'after'; the two words only share letters.
items.cn: medical 追溯到拉丁语 medicus“医生”，不含希腊语成分。method 里的 meta- 是希腊语介词“追寻”，不是现代表示“超越、之后”的前缀；两个词只共享字母。

note.en: The first group is the word family built on method: the adjective, the adverb and the study of method. The second group compares the nouns English uses for 'a way of doing something', which differ in scale and in who owns the way.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在 method 上的词族：形容词、副词与研究方法的学问。第二组比较英语里表示“做某事的方式”的几个名词，区别在于尺度大小与“这条路归谁”。

entries.definition: the branch of knowledge that studies methods, or the set of methods used in a field. It is not a longer synonym of method: a methodology can contain several methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究方法的学问分支，或某一领域所使用的一套方法。它不是 method 的加长同义词：一套方法论里可以包含好几种方法。

entries.definition: done according to a method; orderly and systematic. It describes a person or a procedure, not a route.
entries.definitionCN: 按方法进行的；有条理、有系统的。它描述人或程序，而不描述一条路线。

entries.definition: in an orderly, step-by-step way. It answers 'how', while method answers 'by what route'.
entries.definitionCN: 有条理地、一步一步地。它回答“怎样做”，而 method 回答“走哪条路”。

entries.definition: to reduce something to order or system. The verb turns the noun into an action; it is rare outside formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物整理成秩序或体系。这个动词把名词变成动作；在正式写作之外很少见。

entries.definition: a way of dealing with a problem or subject, often including the attitude behind it. It is broader and softer than method, which implies explicit steps.
entries.definitionCN: 处理问题或课题的方式，常包含背后的态度。它比 method 更宽、更软，而 method 暗示明确的步骤。

entries.definition: a particular way of carrying out a single task, especially one requiring skill. Techniques are the small parts inside a method.
entries.definitionCN: 完成单项任务的具体方式，尤指需要技巧的那种。technique 是 method 内部的一个个小零件。

entries.definition: a thing or resource used to achieve an end. Means answers 'with what'; method answers 'in what order'.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到目的而使用的东西或资源。means 回答“用什么”，method 回答“按什么顺序”。

entries.definition: an established or official sequence of steps. It is more bureaucratic than method and often written down by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的或官方的步骤顺序。它比 method 更带行政色彩，常由某个权威写下来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road', the Latin borrowing methodus, and the family methodical, methodology, methodize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”、拉丁语借词 methodus，以及 methodical、methodology、methodize 词族。

normal.en: hodos means 'road'. A method is literally 'a following after on a road': meta plus hodos.
normal.cn: hodos 意为“路”。method 字面上就是“沿路跟随”：meta 加 hodos。

normal.en: In method, meta- does not mean 'beyond' or 'after' as it does in modern English; it means 'in pursuit of'. The Greek preposition is about chasing, not about position.
normal.cn: 在 method 里，meta- 不像现代英语那样表示“超越”或“之后”，而是“追寻”。这个希腊语介词讲的是追赶，不是位置。

normal.en: Methodology is not a fancy word for method: it is the study of methods, or the whole set of them used in a field.
normal.cn: methodology 不是 method 的高级说法：它是对方法的研究，或某一领域所使用的整套方法。

normal.en: Methodical describes the person who always walks on a path; method names the path itself.
normal.cn: methodical 描述那个总沿着路走的人；method 命名的是那条路本身。

normal.en: Medical looks similar but is Latin medicus 'physician'. One word has a road in it, the other has a doctor.
normal.cn: medical 看着像，其实是拉丁语 medicus“医生”。一个词里装着一条路，另一个词里装着一位医生。

abstract.en: Picture grass in a field. One path is visible because many feet chose the same line; that line is a method.
abstract.cn: 想象一片草地。有一条路看得见，是因为许多脚选择了同一条线；那条线就是 method。

abstract.en: A path can be walked by one person or written down for a school. The moment it is written down, method becomes methodology.
abstract.cn: 一条路可以由一个人走，也可以写下来给一个学派。写下来的那一刻，method 就变成了 methodology。

abstract.en: Method is the order of steps, not the tool in your hand. A hammer is a means; how you swing it is a technique; the sequence is the method.
abstract.cn: method 是步骤的顺序，不是你手里的工具。锤子是 means；怎么挥是 technique；先后次序才是 method。

examples.en: No method will save a study that was badly designed in the first place.
examples.cn: 如果一项研究一开始就设计得很糟，任何方法都救不了它。

examples.en: She works without method, yet somehow finishes before everyone else.
examples.cn: 她做事毫无章法，却总能比别人先做完。

examples.en: The two laboratories use different methods and keep getting different numbers.
examples.cn: 两个实验室用不同的方法，得到的数字也一直不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: “卖瑟德”——卖瑟德把一条踩出来的小路画在纸上，卖给后来的人照着走 → method 方法、办法（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自希腊语 methodos“追寻、探究”，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，核心是“沿着一条路追到目标”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of method, all from one image: a line worn into the grass by feet that wanted the same destination. It can be one path, the habit of taking paths, or the written map of them.
sensesIntro.cn: method 的九个义项都来自同一幅画面：一条被想抵达同一目标的脚踩出来的草径。它可以是某一条路、走路的习惯，或被写下来的路线图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path worn into grass, pointing at a destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被踩进草地的小路，指向某个目的地。

branches.en: THE PATH: the oldest senses name a procedure, first for curing disease, then for anything at all.
branches.cn: 路：最老的义项命名一套程序，先用于治病，后用于任何事。

branches.en: THE HABIT: orderliness is walking on a path by choice, and the idiom says a path may hide inside apparent chaos.
branches.cn: 习惯：条理是有意识地沿路走；那条习语则说，混乱里也可能藏着一条路。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: written rules turn a path into a teachable system, and science inherits the oldest 'inquiry' sense.
branches.cn: 体系：写下来的规则把路变成可教的体系，而科学继承的是最古老的“探究”义。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: teaching and acting give the path a proper name, and philosophy makes the pursuit itself a rule.
branches.cn: 学派：教学与表演给这条路一个专名，哲学则把追寻本身变成规则。

branches.en: THE CODE: in software the object still knows a fixed route to take when called.
branches.cn: 代码：在软件里，对象被调用时仍知道该走哪条固定路线。

intro.en: Method is a Greek compound borrowed whole: meta- plus hodos 'road'. English adds -ical, -ically, -ology, -ologist and -ize, while the same hodos builds episode, period and Exodus.
intro.cn: method 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：meta- 加 hodos“路”。英语加上 -ical、-ically、-ology、-ologist、-ize，而同一个 hodos 还构成 episode、period、Exodus。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek word unchanged as methodus 'way of teaching or going', and Late Latin methodicus came from Greek methodikos. Latin had its own word for 'way', modus, but method did not come from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语原样吸收希腊词作 methodus“教学或行走之道”，晚期拉丁语 methodicus 来自希腊语 methodikos。拉丁语自己表示“方式”的词是 modus，但 method 并非来自它。

items.meaning: a following after on a road; a way of doing something
items.meaningCN: 沿路追寻；做某事的方法（meta- 追寻 + hodos 路）
items.example: They tried every method and failed with each.
items.exampleCN: 他们试了每一种方法，每一种都失败了。

items.meaningCN: 按方法进行的；有条理的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: His methodical notes filled four notebooks.
items.exampleCN: 他条理分明的笔记写满了四个本子。

items.meaningCN: 有条理地；一步一步地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She checked each drawer methodically.
items.exampleCN: 她逐个抽屉有条理地检查。

items.meaning: the study of methods; a set of methods used in a field
items.meaningCN: 方法论；一套研究方法（-ology 表学问）
items.example: The paper was rejected for its weak methodology.
items.exampleCN: 这篇论文因方法论薄弱而被拒。

items.example: The two studies differ on methodological grounds.
items.exampleCN: 这两项研究在方法上存在分歧。

items.meaning: a specialist in methods of research
items.example: A methodologist was added to the review panel.
items.exampleCN: 评审组里增加了一位方法论专家。

items.meaning: to arrange according to a system
items.meaningCN: 使有条理；使系统化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: He methodized the archive over one winter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一个冬天把档案整理成体系。

items.meaning: a member of the Protestant denomination founded at Oxford in 1729
items.meaningCN: 卫理公会教徒（-ist 表追随者，源于其讲究方法的修行方式）
items.example: The Methodist chapel still stands on the corner.
items.exampleCN: 卫理公会礼拜堂仍立在街角。

items.structure: epi- (besides) + eisodos (a coming in, from hodos 'way')
items.meaning: an incident or instalment inserted into a larger whole
items.meaningCN: 插曲；（系列中的）一集（epi- 另外 + eisodos 进入，含 hodos 路）
items.example: The final episode answers nothing.
items.exampleCN: 最后一集什么也没解答。

items.meaning: a going round; a length of time
items.meaningCN: 周期；一段时间（peri- 环绕 + hodos 路，即“绕一圈”）
items.example: The period lasted almost a century.
items.exampleCN: 这一时期持续了将近一个世纪。

items.meaning: a going out; a mass departure
items.meaningCN: 出走；大批离去（ex- 向外 + hodos 路）
items.example: The drought set off an exodus from the villages.
items.exampleCN: 旱灾引发了村庄的大批出走。

items.meaning: a performance technique that draws on the actor's own experience
items.meaningCN: 方法派表演（以体系命名的表演技术）
items.example: Method acting changed how American films were shot.
items.exampleCN: 方法派表演改变了美国电影的拍摄方式。

definition_zh: 有权使用；可以接触；能够获得；可以进入；有……的通道
definition_en: to be able or entitled to reach, use or obtain something, whether a place, a service, information or a person
core_image: 一道闸门半开，门禁灯由红转绿，持卡人推门而入，里面的一排书架与资料柜都向他敞开
scene: 阅览室门口，管理员核对了证件，把一张临时卡递给来访的学生，告诉他哪些书架可以自己去取。 Only enrolled students may have access to the closed stacks.
sceneCN: 这里指被允许进入并使用特定资源（第 1 个义项：有权使用某处资源或设施）；句意为只有注册在籍的学生才可以使用闭架书库。图中可辨识物件：门禁读卡器、临时卡、闭架书库、管理员证。

pos.zh: 有权使用；能够获得（及物动词短语，后接资源、服务或信息）
可以进入；可以接近（后接场所、人群或机构）

derivatives.zh: 短语中的核心名词兼动词，义为「通道；使用权；进入」
由名词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可接近的；易理解的」
由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「可及性；可达性」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「就任；加入；入藏」
由动词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「被访问过的」

senses.title: Entitled to use a resource
senses.definition: to have the right or the means to use a facility or a supply
senses.definitionCN: 拥有使用某项设施或供应的权利或条件
senses.example: Every resident should have access to clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 每位居民都应能获得清洁用水。
senses.why: The core verb meant to go near, and a right of use is a door left open for one to approach.
senses.whyCN: 核心动词本义是「走近」，而使用权就是一扇为你留着、让你靠近的门。

senses.title: Able to reach information
senses.definition: to be able to consult records, data or documents
senses.definitionCN: 能够查阅记录、数据或文件
senses.example: Researchers may have access to the archive only with written permission.
senses.exampleCN: 研究人员只有获得书面许可，才可以查阅该档案。
senses.why: A record room is entered by permission, and the way in is the permission.
senses.whyCN: 记录室凭许可进入，而那条进去的路就是许可。

senses.title: Able to obtain care
senses.definition: to be able to reach and receive medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 能够到达并接受医疗
senses.example: Rural families should have access to a clinic within an hour's drive.
senses.exampleCN: 农村家庭应能在一小时车程内获得诊所服务。
senses.why: A clinic within an hour is a door that can actually be reached.
senses.whyCN: 一小时车程内的诊所，是一扇真正够得着的门。

senses.title: Able to receive education
senses.definition: to be able to attend and use schools or courses
senses.definitionCN: 能够进入并使用学校或课程
senses.example: Girls in the district can have access to the same schools as boys.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的女孩可以和男孩进入同样的学校。
senses.why: A school place is a door held open for a child.
senses.whyCN: 一个学位，是为孩子留着的一扇门。

senses.title: Able to reach a place
senses.definition: to have a route by which a place can be reached
senses.definitionCN: 拥有通往某处的路径
senses.example: The upper valley may have access to the sea through one narrow pass.
senses.exampleCN: 上游河谷可能通过一个狭窄山口通向大海。
senses.why: This is the physical layer: access as a way in, before it became a right.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理层面：先有「进去的路」，后来才有「进去的权利」。

senses.title: Hold the right to enter
senses.definition: to be permitted to enter a restricted place
senses.definitionCN: 被允许进入受限制的场所
senses.example: Only two technicians should have access to the sealed room.
senses.exampleCN: 只有两名技师应被允许进入那间密封室。
senses.why: Two keyholders are two keys to the same locked door.
senses.whyCN: 两个持钥人，就是同一扇锁门上的两把钥匙。

senses.title: Able to use samples or records
senses.definition: to be allowed to handle material kept for research
senses.definitionCN: 被允许接触为研究保存的材料
senses.example: Visiting scholars can have access to the fossil collection.
senses.exampleCN: 访问学者可以使用这批化石藏品。
senses.why: A fossil collection opens to visiting scholars by written permission.
senses.whyCN: 化石藏品凭书面许可向访问学者敞开。

senses.title: Able to enter a market
senses.definition: to be allowed to sell or compete in a market
senses.definitionCN: 被允许在某一市场销售或竞争
senses.example: Small exporters may have access to the regional market under the new terms.
senses.exampleCN: 小型出口商在新条款下可能获得区域市场准入。
senses.why: A market door opens to exporters when the terms admit them.
senses.whyCN: 条款准许时，市场之门向出口商打开。

senses.title: Able to reach decision makers
senses.definition: to be able to meet or speak with people who decide
senses.definitionCN: 能够见到或向做决定的人表达
senses.example: Local groups should have access to the officials who set the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 本地团体应能接触到制定预算的官员。
senses.why: A local group that can sit with budget makers has reached the inner door.
senses.whyCN: 能与编预算者同坐的本地团体，已经走到内门。

intro.en: The phrase joins the native verb of holding to a Latin noun built from to plus going. Access is first a way of going near, and the phrase turns that way into a capacity, a permission or a right.
intro.cn: 这个短语把本族表示「持有」的动词，与拉丁语中由「向」加「行走」构成的名词结合。通道首先是「走近的路」，短语则把这条路变成能力、许可或权利。

items.en: Cedere meant to go, to move, to yield, and it stands behind proceed, concede and exceed.
items.cn: 这个词意为「走、移动、让出」，行进、让步与超过诸词都由它而来。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus cedere produced accedere, to go near, to approach, to come to.
items.cn: 表示「朝向」的前缀加「走」，构成「走近、接近、来到」的动词。

items.en: The noun named a coming near, a way of approach, and later a fit or an attack of illness.
items.cn: 相应的名词指「走近、接近之路」，后来也指疾病的发作。

items.en: English took the noun for a way in or an approach, and the right of entry came later.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个名词，指「入口、接近」，表示「进入的权利」的用法后来才出现。

items.en: With the native verb of holding, the phrase came to cover both permission and practical ability. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 与本族「持有」动词结合后，这个短语兼指许可与实际能力。最早书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin going word; the second group holds other ways of saying that something can be reached or used.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「行走」之词；第二组是其他表示「可以到达或使用」的说法。

entries.definition: It names the way in or the right itself, as in a service with wide access; the phrase puts a holder in front of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指「入口」或「权利」本身，如覆盖面广的服务；短语则在它前面加上持有者。

entries.definition: It describes a place or a text that can be reached or understood; it is a property, not a possession.
entries.definitionCN: 形容某地或某文本可达、可懂；它是性质，不是谁持有之物。

entries.definition: It means coming to office or adding to a collection, not the ability to use something.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「就任」或「入藏」，而不是「使用的能力」。

entries.tag: same latin going verb different pr
entries.definition: From beyond plus going: it means to go past a limit, sharing the root but not the sense of entry.
entries.definitionCN: 由「越过」加「走」构成，意为「超出限度」，共享词根，却不含「进入」。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for having the capacity to use something; it says nothing about permission.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素表示「有能力使用」，不涉及许可。

entries.definition: It stresses a right that can be claimed, often in law or policy, without the physical sense of entry.
entries.definitionCN: 强调可主张的权利，常用于法律或政策，不含物理上的进入。

entries.definition: A general verb for getting to a place or a person; it lacks the sense of a granted right.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指到达某地或找到某人，不含「被授予的权利」。

entries.definition: It focuses on the act of getting in through a door or a barrier, closer to the physical senses.
entries.definitionCN: 强调穿过门或障碍进去的动作，较接近物理义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the gate reader, the closed stacks, the rural clinic and the narrow pass.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用门禁读卡器、闭架书库、乡村诊所与狭窄山口四个场景。

normal.en: A gate half open, a light turning from red to green, a reader passing a card.
normal.cn: 闸门半开，指示灯由红转绿，读卡人递过一张卡。

normal.en: A student handed a temporary card and told which shelves are open to her.
normal.cn: 学生拿到一张临时卡，被告知哪些书架向她开放。

normal.en: A village an hour from the nearest clinic, and a road that makes the hour possible.
normal.cn: 村庄离最近诊所一小时车程，而这条路让这一小时成为可能。

normal.en: One narrow pass between the upper valley and the sea.
normal.cn: 上游河谷与大海之间，只有一道狭窄山口。

normal.en: A local group sitting in the same room as the officials who set the budget.
normal.cn: 本地团体与编预算的官员，坐在同一间屋里。

abstract.en: Access is a door plus a key: the door alone is only a route.
abstract.cn: 可及性是门加钥匙：只有门，那只是路。

abstract.en: The same word covers a right and a road, because both decide who may come near.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指权利也指道路，因为两者都决定谁能靠近。

abstract.en: What is open to everyone stops being a privilege and becomes an infrastructure.
abstract.cn: 对所有人开放之后，特权就变成了基础设施。

examples.en: Every patient should have access to a copy of the record held about them.
examples.cn: 每位患者都应有权拿到关于自己的记录副本。

examples.en: Small firms may have access to the fund only through a local bank.
examples.cn: 小公司可能只能通过本地银行获得这笔基金。

examples.en: The public can have access to the gardens on two days each month.
examples.cn: 公众每月有两天可以进入这些花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「哈夫 阿克塞斯 图」：把「走近」记成闸门红灯转绿、刷卡进门——门开了，路就通了

root: 前半为本族动词，意为「持有」；后半名词出自拉丁语，由表示「朝向」的前缀加表示「行走」的动词构成，本义是「走近、接近之路」，后引申为「进入的权利」。短语兼指许可与实际能力。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a right to a road: water, information, care, schooling, a pass to the sea, a sealed room, a fossil collection, a market and a minister's door.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从权利走到道路：水、信息、医疗、教育、通海的山口、密封室、化石藏品、市场与官员的门。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate half open, the reader turning green, a card passed, and the shelves beyond opening to the holder.
core.cn: 核心意象：闸门半开，读卡器转绿，卡片递过，里面的书架向持卡人敞开。

branches.en: THE BASIC NEED: water, care and schooling are rights before they are routes.
branches.cn: 基本所需：水、医疗与教育，先被当作权利，然后才被当作道路。

branches.en: THE RECORD ROOM: an archive and a fossil collection open only to those with permission.
branches.cn: 记录室：档案馆与化石藏品，只对获准者开放。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL GATE: a pass to the sea, a sealed room with two keyholders.
branches.cn: 物理的门：通海的山口，只有两名持钥者的密封室。

branches.en: THE MARKET DOOR: an exporter admitted to a regional market under new terms.
branches.cn: 市场之门：出口商在新条款下被准入区域市场。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL DOOR: a local group able to sit with those who set the budget.
branches.cn: 官员之门：本地团体能与编预算者同坐一室。

intro.en: The family is built on a Latin going verb with a prefix of approach; the endings name the way in, the quality of being reachable and the act of entering office.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语「行走」动词上，前缀表示「朝向」；词尾命名入口、可达的性质与就任的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin accedere and accessus passed through French into English, which added its own adjective and noun endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「走近」动词与名词经法语进入英语，英语加上自己的形容词与名词词尾。

items.example: It marks the movement as coming near.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「走近」这一移动。

items.example: The going verb at the base.
items.exampleCN: 底层的「行走」动词。

items.example: The direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a coming near, a way of approach
items.example: The noun English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入的名词。

items.example: It forms the adjective for what can be reached.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「可达」的形容词。

items.example: It forms the noun of reachability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「可达性」的名词。

items.example: It forms the noun of coming to office.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「就任」的名词。

items.example: It points the access at what is reached.
items.exampleCN: 它把「可及」指向所达之物。

derivatives.zh: 核心名词兼动词，义为「通道；使用权」
由名词加「可……的」词尾构成，义为「可接近的」
由形容词加名词尾构成，义为「可及性」
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「就任；入藏」

definition_zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚；（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆；不利后果；代价
definition_en: a punishment or disadvantage imposed for breaking a rule, failing a standard, or gaining an unfair advantage
core_image: 裁判在记分牌上划掉犯规一方的一分，再让对方站到更有利的位置上
scene: 足球场上，后卫在禁区里从背后绊倒对方前锋，裁判指向点球点，并向犯规者出示黄牌。 The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
sceneCN: 这里指「体育比赛中因犯规而判给对方的一次罚球」，对应第 4 个义项：犯规之后由对方在固定位置主罚的一脚；句意为后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。画面要点：禁区线、点球点、裁判手中的黄牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 处罚；罚款；刑罚（可数，常与 impose、pay、face 连用）
（体育）点球、罚球；罚杆（可数，足球、橄榄球、高尔夫常用）

derivatives.zh: 与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经形容词 poenalis 进入英语 → 由「那笔罚」转为形容「与刑罚有关的性质」
由 penal 加动词后缀（经法语与拉丁语，表「使……化」）→ 语义由「属于刑罚的」转为「施加处罚这一动作」
由 penalize 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「施加处罚」转为「被处罚的过程或状态」
penalty 加复数后缀 → 由一次处罚转为多起、多类处罚
与 penalty 同出拉丁 poena，经动词 punire 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「罚金」转为「以惩罚为目的、带有惩罚性质的」

senses.title: A punishment for a breach
senses.titleCN: 因违反规则而受的处罚
senses.definition: a punishment imposed on a person or group that has broken a rule or failed a duty
senses.definitionCN: 对违反规则或未尽义务的个人与团体所施加的惩罚
senses.example: The league imposed a heavy penalty on the club for breaching the salary cap.
senses.exampleCN: 联盟因该俱乐部违反工资上限而对其处以重罚。
senses.why: Latin poena named the price exacted after a wrong, so the word begins as the consequence that follows a fault, not as the fault itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 poena 指犯错之后被索取的代价，所以这个词从一开始就是过错之后随之而来的后果，而不是过错本身。

senses.title: Money exacted for an offence
senses.titleCN: 为违法行为缴纳的钱款
senses.definition: a sum of money that an offender is required to pay to the authority that recorded the offence
senses.definitionCN: 违法者必须向记录该行为的机关缴纳的一笔钱
senses.example: Drivers face a penalty of two hundred pounds for using a phone at the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 司机开车时使用手机，将面临两百英镑的罚款。
senses.why: Since poena also meant the compensation handed over to settle a wrong, the abstract consequence could be counted out in coins.
senses.whyCN: 因为 poena 也指为平息过错而交出的补偿，这种抽象的后果便可以用钱币数出来。

senses.title: A punishment fixed in statute
senses.definition: the punishment that a law prescribes for a particular offence, usually stated as a maximum
senses.definitionCN: 法律为某一具体罪行规定的惩罚，通常以最高刑期或最高数额表述
senses.example: The statute carries a maximum penalty of ten years in prison.
senses.exampleCN: 该法条规定的最高刑罚是十年监禁。
senses.why: When a community writes the price of a wrong into a code, the word shifts from the verdict spoken in court to the number printed in the law book.
senses.whyCN: 当共同体把过错的代价写进法典，这个词就从法庭上宣读的判决，转为法律文本里印着的那个数目。

senses.title: A free shot awarded for a foul
senses.titleCN: 因犯规而判给对方的罚球
senses.definition: an advantage given to the opposing side in a sport because the other side broke a rule
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛中因一方犯规而判给另一方的有利机会
senses.example: The referee awarded a penalty after the defender tripped the striker inside the box.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫在禁区内绊倒前锋后，裁判判给了点球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal word because a foul must be paid for; here the payment takes the form of an unopposed shot from a marked spot.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律用词，因为犯规必须付出代价；在这里，代价的形式是在固定点上无人防守的一脚射门。

senses.title: A stroke added in golf
senses.titleCN: 高尔夫中被加罚的一杆
senses.definition: an extra stroke added to a player's score as a punishment for a mistake on the course
senses.definitionCN: 球场上因失误而被加进球员成绩里的一杆
senses.example: His ball found the water, so he took a penalty and dropped again.
senses.exampleCN: 他的球落进水里，于是他接受罚杆后重新抛球。
senses.why: Golf counts strokes instead of money, so paying for a mistake means adding a stroke to your own card.
senses.whyCN: 高尔夫数的是杆数而不是钱，所以为失误付出代价，就是在自己的记分卡上多加一杆。

senses.title: A charge for breaking a contract
senses.titleCN: 违反合同条款应付的违约金
senses.definition: an amount that a contract requires one party to pay if it acts in a way the agreement forbids
senses.definitionCN: 合同要求一方在做出协议禁止的行为时支付的款项
senses.example: Early repayment of the loan triggers a penalty of one month's interest.
senses.exampleCN: 提前偿还贷款会触发相当于一个月利息的违约金。
senses.why: A contract fixes in advance what a breach will cost, turning the older idea of compensation into a clause with a stated figure.
senses.whyCN: 合同事先定明违约要花多少钱，把较早的「补偿」观念变成一条写着具体数目的条款。

senses.title: The price of an advantage
senses.definition: a disadvantage that comes with a privilege or a success rather than with a rule broken
senses.definitionCN: 伴随特权或成功而来的不利之处，而不是因违规招致的
senses.example: Fame brought her the penalty of constant scrutiny.
senses.exampleCN: 名气给她带来了被人时刻审视的代价。
senses.why: If every gain carries a price, then even a privilege can carry a penalty, although no rule has been broken.
senses.whyCN: 如果每一种获得都带着价码，那么连特权也能带上「罚」，尽管并没有谁违规。

senses.title: A handicap laid on a contestant
senses.titleCN: 加在参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.definition: a disadvantage imposed on a competitor in order to equalize unequal starting points
senses.definitionCN: 为使不相等的起跑条件趋于平衡而加在某位参赛者身上的不利条件
senses.example: The older runners started with a time penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 年长的跑者带着时间上的不利条件起跑。
senses.why: Any contest that tries to balance unequal starting points can turn punishment into a handicap placed on the stronger side.
senses.whyCN: 凡是试图平衡起跑差距的比赛，都能把「罚」变成加在占优一方身上的不利条件。

intro.en: Penalty comes from Latin poena 'penalty, punishment, compensation', itself a loan from Greek poine 'price paid for a wrong'. Through Old French penalite it entered English law. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: penalty 出自拉丁语 poena「处罚、惩罚、补偿」，而 poena 又借自希腊语 poine「为过错付出的代价」；它经古法语 penalite 进入英语法律用语。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Poine named the price that settled a wrong, whether blood-money paid to a family or a fine owed to a community.
items.cn: poine 指为平息过错而付出的价，既可以是赔给家族的偿命钱，也可以是交给共同体的罚金。

items.en: Poena kept both halves of that idea: the punishment itself and the sum handed over in compensation.
items.cn: poena 保留了这个观念的两半：处罚本身，以及作为补偿交出的那笔钱。

items.en: The adjective poenalis 'of punishment' produced English penal and later supplied the stem for penalize.
items.cn: 形容词 poenalis 意为「与处罚有关的」，它生成英语的 penal，后来又提供了 penalize 的词干。

items.en: Legal French used penalite for the punishment attached to an offence, and Middle English took the word in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法律法语用 penalite 指附在某一罪行上的处罚，中古英语在十五世纪吸收了这个词。

items.en: Penalty first named a punishment in law, then any sum exacted, then any disadvantage fixed by an agreement.
items.cn: penalty 最初指法律上的处罚，随后指任何被索取的钱款，再后来指协议定下的任何不利后果。

items.en: Nineteenth-century football rules turned the word into the name of the kick itself, and golf gave it the sense of an added stroke.
items.cn: 十九世纪的足球规则把这个词变成那脚罚球本身的名称，高尔夫又赋予它「加罚一杆」的意思。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the same Latin stem plus one mere look-alike; the second group offers near alternatives for a punishment or a burden.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干的词，外加一个只是长得像的词；第二组是「处罚或负担」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of punishment'; it describes the legal character of a measure, not the measure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「刑罚的」的形容词；它描述一项措施的惩罚性质，而不指这项措施本身。

entries.definition: The verb built on penal; it names the act of imposing what a penalty names as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 由 penal 构成的动词；penalty 指那件被施加的罚，这个动词则指施加的动作。

entries.definition: Formed from Latin punire rather than directly from poena; it stresses the intention to punish.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁动词 punire 而非直接由 poena 构成；它强调「意在惩罚」这一层。

entries.definition: A small room where food is kept; it merely looks like penalty in spelling and is not related to it in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 存放食物的小房间；只是拼写与 penalty 相似，并非同源。

entries.definition: A sum paid as punishment for an offence; it covers the money sense but not the sporting or contractual ones.
entries.definitionCN: 因违法而缴纳的一笔钱；它只覆盖金钱义，不覆盖体育与合同义。

entries.definition: A penalty applied by an authority to enforce a rule; broader in politics and diplomacy, narrower in sport.
entries.definitionCN: 权威为执行规则而施加的处罚；在政治与外交中范围更广，在体育中范围更窄。

entries.definition: Something lost by rule because of a fault; it stresses what is taken away rather than what is imposed.
entries.definitionCN: 因过错而按规则失去的东西；它强调被拿走的东西，而不是被施加的东西。

entries.definition: A disadvantage placed on a stronger competitor; it matches the sporting sense but carries no blame.
entries.definitionCN: 加在较强竞争者身上的不利条件；与体育义相合，但不含责备。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的派生词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Poena is the Latin word for the price of a wrong; a penalty is that price written down.
normal.cn: poena 是拉丁语中「过错的代价」，penalty 就是把这笔代价写下来。

normal.en: The same family runs through penal, penalize and punitive, all keeping the idea of a price to be paid.
normal.cn: 同一词族贯穿 penal、penalize 与 punitive，都保留「要付代价」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases lock the senses: death penalty, penalty kick, penalty clause.
normal.cn: 固定搭配锁定义项：死刑、点球、违约金条款。

normal.en: A penalty is always owed to someone: a referee, a court or a contract.
normal.cn: 罚总是欠着某一方的：裁判、法庭或合同。

normal.en: If no rule was broken and nothing is owed, there is no penalty.
normal.cn: 若无人违规、无所亏欠，就谈不上罚。

abstract.en: Picture a coin box beside a rulebook, and every broken rule drops a coin in.
abstract.cn: 想象规则手册旁放着一只钱箱，每破一条规则就投进一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a runner made to stand two steps behind the line because he started too early.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者因为抢跑，被要求站到起跑线后两步。

abstract.en: Picture a hill of trophies with a small toll gate at the foot, charging every winner.
abstract.cn: 想象一座由奖杯堆成的山，山脚设着一道小收费站，向每位赢家收费。

examples.en: The court added a penalty for the delay in reporting the accident.
examples.cn: 法院因事故报告延误而加判了一笔处罚。

examples.en: A penalty shoot-out decided the final.
examples.cn: 点球决胜决定了决赛的归属。

examples.en: There is a penalty for paying the loan back early.
examples.cn: 提前还贷是要付违约金的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派人提」——你一犯规，就派人来提走一笔钱 → 罚款、处罚

root: 希腊 poine「为过错付出的价」→ 拉丁 poena「处罚、补偿」→ 拉丁形容词 poenalis → 古法语 penalite → 英语 penalty；同族词有 penal、penalize、punitive、punish。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses rest on one move: a wrong creates a debt, and the debt is collected. The collection may be a punishment, a sum of money, a statutory sentence, a shot at goal, a golf stroke, a contractual charge, the price of privilege, or a handicap in a race.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立于同一个动作：过错生出一笔债，这笔债要被收回。收回的形式可以是一次处罚、一笔钱、一条法定刑、一脚罚球、一杆罚杆、一项合同收费、特权的代价，或比赛中的不利条件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a referee striking one point off the offender's side and moving the other side forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁判从犯规一方的记分上划掉一分，再把另一方往前挪。

branches.en: LEGAL CONSEQUENCE: a fault creates a debt that a verdict or a statute collects in the form of punishment.
branches.cn: 法律后果：过错生出一笔债，由判决或法典以处罚的形式把它收回。

branches.en: MONEY FORM: the debt is counted in coins, from a fine owed to a public authority to a charge written into a contract.
branches.cn: 金钱形式：这笔债用钱币计算，从欠公共机关的一笔罚金到写进合同的一项收费。

branches.en: SPORTING FORM: the payment becomes an uncontested shot at goal or an extra stroke on the card.
branches.cn: 体育形式：这笔代价变成一脚无人防守的射门，或记分卡上多加的一杆。

branches.en: VOLUNTARY PRICE: a privilege or a success brings its own burden, although no rule was broken.
branches.cn: 自愿的代价：特权或成功自带负担，尽管并没有人违规。

branches.en: EQUALIZING BURDEN: a contest lays a disadvantage on the stronger side to level the start.
branches.cn: 平衡的负担：比赛把不利条件加在占优一方，使起跑趋于齐平。

intro.en: Penalty is a noun from the poena family; its Latin adjective and its related verb branch into several English words about punishment.
intro.cn: penalty 是 poena 词族中的名词；它的拉丁形容词与相关动词分出了若干与惩罚有关的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena and poenalis give penal, penalty and penalize, while Latin punire, built on poena, gives punish, punishment and punitive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena 与 poenalis 生出 penal、penalty 与 penalize；由 poena 构成的拉丁 punire 则生出 punish、punishment 与 punitive。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of a debt owed after a fault.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干带着「犯错之后欠下一笔债」的意思。

items.example: The referee awarded a penalty.
items.exampleCN: 裁判判了一个点球。

items.example: The new law raised the penalties for dumping waste.
items.exampleCN: 新法提高了倾倒废弃物的处罚。

items.example: The country still keeps a penal code.
items.exampleCN: 该国仍然保留着一部刑法典。

items.example: The rules penalize late filing.
items.exampleCN: 规则对逾期提交予以处罚。

items.meaning: the act or state of being punished
items.example: He objected to the penalization of small firms.
items.exampleCN: 他反对对小企业施加处罚。

items.example: The measure was more punitive than preventive.
items.exampleCN: 这项措施更偏向惩罚，而非预防。

items.meaning: to make someone suffer for a wrong
items.example: The court punished the driver.
items.exampleCN: 法庭处罚了那名司机。

items.meaning: the suffering imposed for a wrong
items.meaningCN: 因过错而被施加的痛苦
items.example: The punishment was a month without pay.
items.exampleCN: 处罚是停薪一个月。

items.example: Such conduct is punishable by law.
items.exampleCN: 这种行为依法应受处罚。

latinEntries.meaning: to punish; to exact a penalty

definition_zh: 配额；定额；限额；（按比例分得的）份额
definition_en: a fixed share or amount assigned to a person, group or country, often acting as a limit
core_image: 一只大桶被分成若干等份，每只杯子只准取走贴着自己名字的那一份，多一滴也不行
scene: 合作社的分配会上，会计把全年的收购总量摊到各户，规定每户只能交售属于自己那一份的数量。 At the cooperative meeting the accountant gave each household its quota of the yearly harvest.
sceneCN: 这里指「按规则分得的份额」，对应第 1 个义项：经事先划分后归某一方的定量；句意为会计在会上把全年收购量按户分配，每户只交售自己那一份。画面要点：分配桌、名册、等分的大桶。

pos.zh: 配额；定额；限额（可数，常与 import、sales、immigration 等连用）

derivatives.zh: 多份配额（quota 加复数后缀，语义由单份转为多份）
配额制度（quota 与 system 构成的复合词，指成套的配额安排）
配额抽样（quota 与 sampling 构成的复合术语，指按配额填格的抽样法）
以配额为基础的（quota 加 based 构成的复合形容词，指以配额为运作依据）
不受配额限制的（quota 加 free 构成的复合形容词，指免除配额约束）

senses.title: A share fixed by prior division
senses.titleCN: 事先划分后归某一方的定量
senses.definition: the part of a total that is measured out and assigned to one person or group in advance
senses.definitionCN: 总量中经事先量出并分配给某一个人或群体的那部分
senses.example: At the cooperative meeting the accountant gave each household its quota of the yearly harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 分配会上，会计把全年收购量按户分配，每户得到自己那一份。
senses.why: The Latin source is quota pars, literally 'how great a part', built on quot 'how many', so the word begins as a question about size answered by a fixed number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源是 quota pars，字面为「多大的一份」，由 quot「多少」构成；这个词最初就是对大小的提问，答案是一个定数。

senses.title: An official ceiling on imports
senses.titleCN: 官方设定的进口数量上限
senses.definition: a limit set by a government on the quantity of a good that may be imported
senses.definitionCN: 政府规定的某类商品可以进口的数量上限
senses.example: The government placed a quota on imported steel.
senses.exampleCN: 政府对进口钢材设定了配额。
senses.why: Once a share is fixed by authority rather than by custom, it stops being an entitlement and becomes a wall that trade cannot pass.
senses.whyCN: 当份额由官方而不是惯例来确定，它就不再是应得之份，而变成贸易越不过的一道墙。

senses.title: A required output target
senses.titleCN: 必须完成的产量或销售定额
senses.definition: the amount of work, output or sales that a worker or team is required to reach
senses.definitionCN: 要求员工或团队达到的工作量、产量或销售量
senses.example: Sales staff must meet a monthly quota before bonuses are paid.
senses.exampleCN: 销售人员必须先完成月度定额才能拿到奖金。
senses.why: The same fixed number can be read from below: what was a ceiling for imports becomes a floor that output must reach.
senses.whyCN: 同一个定数也可以从下方读：进口的上限，反过来成了产出必须够到的下限。

senses.title: A limit on the number admitted
senses.definition: the maximum number of people allowed into a country, school or programme in a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一定时期内允许进入某国、某校或某项目的最多人数
senses.example: The university keeps a quota for students from overseas.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学为海外学生保留了固定名额。
senses.why: Counting people rather than goods needs the same instrument: a number agreed beforehand keeps demand from overflowing the gate.
senses.whyCN: 数人与数货物需要同一种工具：事先商定的数字，使需求不会把门挤破。

senses.title: A fixed contribution owed by a member
senses.definition: the set portion of a common cost or supply that each member is obliged to provide
senses.definitionCN: 共同费用或物资中每一成员必须承担的那一份
senses.example: Each branch pays its quota of the association's running costs.
senses.exampleCN: 每个分会承担协会运转费用中属于自己的那一份。
senses.why: When the direction of the flow reverses, the assigned part turns into an obligation: the member owes the number instead of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 当流向反转，被分配的那一份就变成义务：成员不再是领取这个数字，而是欠下这个数字。

senses.title: A proportional share of posts or seats
senses.titleCN: 按比例保留的席位或职位
senses.definition: a number of places reserved for a category of people in an assembly, workforce or list
senses.definitionCN: 在议会、员工队伍或名单中为某类人预留的席位数
senses.example: The party reserved a quota of seats for women candidates.
senses.exampleCN: 该党为女性候选人保留了固定比例的席位。
senses.why: Division by proportion is the oldest use of the word, and reserved seats are simply that proportion written into a rulebook.
senses.whyCN: 按比例划分是这个词最古老的用法，保留席位不过是把这一比例写进了规则手册。

senses.title: Quota sampling in research
senses.definition: a sampling method that fills each category of a population up to a preset number
senses.definitionCN: 按预设数目把总体中每一类填满的抽样方法
senses.example: The survey used quota sampling to fill each age band.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查用配额抽样填满各个年龄段。
senses.why: Statistics borrowed the word because the sample is built the way a shipment is built: each cell gets exactly its assigned count.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用这个词，因为样本的搭建方式如同配货：每个格子里都正好放进被分配的数量。

senses.title: Any measured portion, even of non-material things
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：连非实体之物也被量出的那一份
senses.definition: an allotted amount of something abstract, such as luck, patience or misfortune
senses.definitionCN: 某种抽象之物（如运气、耐心或不幸）被分定的量
senses.example: Every generation seems to have its quota of hardship.
senses.exampleCN: 每一代人似乎都有自己那一份艰难。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the arithmetic but drops the goods: whatever can be counted out can also be allotted.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了算术，却去掉了货物：凡能被数出来的东西，也都能被分配。

intro.en: Quota is Latin for 'how great a part'. It is the feminine of quotus 'of what number', from quot 'how many', and it entered English through legal and commercial counting. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: quota 在拉丁语中意为「多大的一份」，是 quotus「第几、若干」的阴性形式，源头为 quot「多少」；它经法律与商业的计算进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Quot was an indeclinable question word meaning 'how many', used in reckoning and in legal formulas.
items.cn: quot 是一个不变化的疑问词，意为「多少」，用于计算与法律套语。

items.en: Quotus 'of what number, which in order' supplied the adjective, and its feminine quota came to mean the part so numbered.
items.cn: quotus 意为「第几的、若干的」，提供形容词；其阴性形式 quota 后来指被这样编号的那一份。

items.en: Legal and estate records used quota pars, literally 'how great a part', for a share fixed by agreement or custom.
items.cn: 法律与田产记录用 quota pars，字面为「多大的一份」，指按协议或惯例定下的份额。

items.en: English took quota as a proportional share, first in accounts and taxation, then in any fixed allowance.
items.cn: 英语在大约 1600 年吸收 quota 表示按比例分得的份额，最初用于账目与税赋，后泛指任何固定配给。

items.en: Immigration quotas in the 1920s and import quotas in the 1930s fixed the modern sense of an official numerical limit; quota sampling followed from the same counting habit.
items.cn: 1920 年代的移民配额与 1930 年代的进口配额，确定了现代「官方数量上限」这一义；配额抽样则出自同一种计数的习惯。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin counting root but diverged in meaning; the second group offers near alternatives for the idea of an allotted amount.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「计数」词根，但语义已分岔；第二组是「被分配的份额」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: To repeat someone's words or to state a price; it comes from the same counting root but the action is marking or citing, not allotting.
entries.definitionCN: 引用他人的话或报出价格；同出「计数」词根，但动作是标出或引述，而不是分配。

entries.definition: A cited passage or a stated price; the counting root survives only in the idea of marking something down.
entries.definitionCN: 被引用的段落或报出的价格；计数词根只剩「把它标记下来」这一层。

entries.definition: The result of a division; it keeps the 'how many times' question but names an answer in arithmetic, never a share.
entries.definitionCN: 除法所得的结果；它保留「多少次」的提问，但指的是算术答案，从不指份额。

entries.definition: A fixed allowance of food or supplies, from Latin ratio 'reckoning', not from quot; it looks close but belongs to another family.
entries.definitionCN: 食物或物资的定额配给，出自拉丁语 ratio「计算」，并非 quot；形近而属于另一词族。

entries.definition: A portion belonging to one party; it states the division but not that the amount was fixed in advance by an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 属于某一方的部分；它只说划分，不说这个数量是由权威事先定下的。

entries.definition: An amount permitted to a person, often for expenses; it stresses permission rather than proportional division.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某人使用的量，常指费用；它强调许可，而不是按比例划分。

entries.definition: A maximum that may not be exceeded; it captures the limit sense of quota but not the idea of a fair share.
entries.definitionCN: 不得超过的最高限度；它涵盖配额的限额义，但不含「公平一份」的意思。

entries.definition: The process or result of assigning resources; it names the act, while quota names the measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 分配资源的过程或结果；它指动作，而配额指被量出的数额。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real counting root, the real derived words and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「计数」词根、真实的派生词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Quot means 'how many', so quota is the answer to 'how many for you'.
normal.cn: quot 意为「多少」，quota 就是「你那份是多少」的答案。

normal.en: The same root shows in quotient and quotation, both about counting or marking a number.
normal.cn: 同一词根见于 quotient 与 quotation，两者都与计数或标号有关。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the limit sense: import quota, sales quota, immigration quota.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出限额义：进口配额、销售定额、移民配额。

normal.en: A quota is always a count, never a price: it answers how many, not how much money.
normal.cn: 配额总是数量，不是价格：它回答「多少个」，不回答「多少钱」。

normal.en: The word implies that someone has already done the splitting before you arrive.
normal.cn: 这个词隐含：在你到场之前，已经有人把总量分好了。

abstract.en: Picture a pie cut into equal wedges, each wedge tagged with a name before anyone lifts a fork.
abstract.cn: 想象一块馅饼被切成等份，每份在有人动叉之前就贴上了名字。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre with a block of seats roped off, the rope saying who may sit there.
abstract.cn: 想象剧院里有一排座位被绳子围住，绳子说明了谁可以坐。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a gate where a counter clicks once for each person and stops at a set number.
abstract.cn: 想象门口排队，计数器每进一人跳一下，到某个数就停住。

examples.en: The fishing fleet exceeded its annual quota by two thousand tonnes.
examples.cn: 捕鱼船队超出年度配额两千吨。

examples.en: A quota on imports pushed buyers toward domestic suppliers.
examples.cn: 进口配额把买家推向国内供应商。

examples.en: She hit her sales quota three weeks before the quarter ended.
examples.cn: 她在季度结束前三周就完成了销售定额。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「括住一份」——先把总量括成若干份，你只拿写着你名字的那一份 → 配额、定额

root: 拉丁 quot「多少」→ quotus「第几、若干」→ quota（pars）「多大的一份」；英语 quota 即「按规则划出的那一份」，同根词有 quotient、quote、quotation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one act: a total is measured out before it is used. The measured part then becomes an import ceiling, an output target, an admission cap, a member's contribution, a reserved block of seats, a sampling cell and finally any countable allotment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立在一个动作上：总量在被使用之前先被量出。这份量出之物随后成为进口上限、产出目标、准入人数上限、成员应缴份额、保留席位、抽样格子，最后扩展到任何可数的分配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a barrel divided into equal parts, each cup taking only the part marked with its name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只桶被分成等份，每只杯子只取贴着它名字的那一份。

branches.en: BASE SHARE: one measured part of a whole, assigned rather than chosen.
branches.cn: 基础份额：整体中被量出的一份，由他人指派而非自己挑选。

branches.en: LIMIT AND TARGET: the assigned number becomes a wall for imports or a floor for output.
branches.cn: 上限与目标：被指派的数量，对进口是墙，对产出是底线。

branches.en: RULES OF ENTRY: a count of people admitted, or a block of seats reserved by proportion.
branches.cn: 准入规则：限定可进入的人数，或按比例预留一批席位。

branches.en: OBLIGATION: the same number reverses direction and becomes what a member owes.
branches.cn: 义务：同一个数字反转方向，成为成员应缴的部分。

branches.en: COUNTING EXTENDED: sampling fills cells by number, and even hardship can be allotted.
branches.cn: 计数外扩：抽样按数目填格，连艰难也能被分配。

intro.en: Quota is a Latin noun built on a question word, and that question word also built several English terms about numbering.
intro.cn: quota 是由一个疑问词构成的拉丁名词，这个疑问词还构成若干英语中与计数有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin quot 'how many' gives quota, quotient, quote and quotation, though the last two moved from counting to marking and citing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 quot「多少」衍生 quota、quotient、quote 与 quotation，后两者已从计数转向标记与引述。

items.example: The element asks a question about quantity.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分提出的是关于数量的问题。

items.structure: quota (from quota pars, how great a part)
items.example: Each household received its quota.
items.exampleCN: 每户都领到了自己那份配额。

items.example: Import quotas were raised this year.
items.exampleCN: 今年的进口配额提高了。

items.example: Divide the total by six to get the quotient.
items.exampleCN: 把总数除以六得到商。

items.structure: quote (same root, to mark or cite)
items.meaning: to repeat words or state a price
items.example: She quoted the report directly.
items.exampleCN: 她直接引用了那份报告。

items.meaning: a cited passage or a price offer
items.example: The quotation was valid for thirty days.
items.exampleCN: 该报价三十天内有效。

items.example: The speech had one quotable line.
items.exampleCN: 这篇演讲有一句值得引用的话。

items.meaning: a method filling categories by set counts
items.meaningCN: 按设定数目填满类别的抽样方法
items.example: Quota sampling kept the age groups balanced.
items.exampleCN: 配额抽样使各年龄组保持平衡。

latinEntries.meaning: of what number; which in order

latinEntries.structure: quota (feminine of quotus, used as a noun)

definition_zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能；语言运用；（仪式的）进行；表演性
definition_en: the act of staging a work for an audience, the way a person, team, or machine carries out a task, the fulfilling of a duty, or the actual use of language as opposed to underlying knowledge
core_image: 舞台上的动作被观众看见并打分，或机器被推到极限，看它到底能跑多快
scene: 年终评审会上，经理把三条产品线的曲线投在墙上，逐条解释哪一条达标。 The manager put the performance curves of three product lines on the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 performance 是「业绩」（第 2 个义项：个人或组织在工作上取得的成果与表现）；句意：经理把三条产品线的业绩曲线投在墙上；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 表演；演出；表现；业绩；执行；履行；性能

derivatives.zh: 表演；执行；履行；运转
表演者；执行者
施为性的；表演性的
表演性；施为性
表现不佳；业绩低于预期

senses.title: A work staged for an audience
senses.definition: the staging of a play, concert, dance, or other work before an audience, taken as an event or an art
senses.definitionCN: 在观众面前上演戏剧、音乐会、舞蹈或其他作品，作为事件或艺术看待
senses.example: The evening performance sold out two weeks in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 晚场演出提前两周售罄。
senses.why: The Old French source meant 'to complete, to carry through'. A play is complete only when it is carried through in front of people: the script is the plan, performance is the doing.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为“完成、贯彻到底”。一部戏只有在人前贯彻到底才算完成：剧本是计划，performance 是做出来。

senses.title: How well a person or group does
senses.definition: the measured quality of a person's, team's, or organization's work against a standard or expectation
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团队或组织的工作相对于标准或预期的可衡量质量
senses.example: Her performance improved once the targets were made clear.
senses.exampleCN: 目标明确之后，她的表现有所提升。
senses.why: The same carrying-through is now watched by a manager rather than an audience. What matters is not whether the work is beautiful but whether it reaches the mark.
senses.whyCN: 同样是贯彻到底，只是这次看的是经理而不是观众。关键不再是作品美不美，而是它有没有达到标准。

senses.title: The carrying out of a task
senses.definition: the act of executing a task, duty, or function, often with attention to whether it was done at all and done correctly
senses.definitionCN: 执行任务、职责或功能的行为，常关注是否完成以及是否正确完成
senses.example: The performance of the repair took longer than the estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项维修的执行比预估花了更长时间。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense: the plan is carried through. No audience and no score, only the difference between what was supposed to happen and what happened.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的义项：计划被贯彻到底。没有观众也没有评分，只有“本该发生什么”与“实际发生了什么”之间的差别。

senses.title: What a machine can do
senses.definition: the speed, power, or efficiency with which a machine, vehicle, or system operates under test or load
senses.definitionCN: 机器、车辆或系统在测试或负载下运转的速度、功率或效率
senses.example: The engine's performance drops at high altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机在高海拔地区性能会下降。
senses.why: A machine has no will, but it can still be pushed to its limit. Performance becomes the measure of that limit, the carrying-through of metal instead of muscle.
senses.whyCN: 机器没有意志，但仍可被推到极限。performance 成了对这种极限的度量，是金属而非肌肉的贯彻到底。

senses.title: Actual use of language
senses.definition: in linguistics, the actual production and comprehension of speech in real situations, as opposed to the speaker's underlying competence
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中指真实情境中话语的实际产生与理解，相对于说话者底层的语言能力
senses.example: Errors in performance do not prove a lack of competence.
senses.exampleCN: 语言运用中的错误并不能证明缺乏语言能力。
senses.why: Chomsky borrowed the word for the difference between knowing a grammar and using it under pressure. The plan inside the head is competence; the carrying-through in time is performance.
senses.whyCN: 乔姆斯基借这个词区分“懂语法”与“在压力下使用语法”。头脑里的计划是语言能力，时间中的贯彻到底是语言运用。

senses.title: One particular show
senses.definition: a single instance of presenting a work, countable and datable, as in the third performance of a run
senses.definitionCN: 呈现某作品的一次具体实例，可计数、可定时，如巡演中的第三场
senses.example: The Saturday performance was recorded for the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 周六那场演出被录入了档案。
senses.why: A run of a play is many carryings-through. This sense counts them, which is why the word takes a plural and a date while the art sense does not.
senses.whyCN: 一部戏的连演是许多次贯彻到底。这个义项把它们数出来，所以这个词可以有复数和日期，而艺术义则不行。

senses.title: The carrying out of a ritual
senses.definition: the enactment of a ceremony, rite, or formal role according to prescribed words and actions
senses.definitionCN: 按规定的言语与动作进行仪式、典礼或正式角色
senses.example: The performance of the wedding rite lasted forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼仪式的进行持续了四十分钟。
senses.why: A rite exists only when it is done. Here performance is not entertainment but the condition of the thing existing at all, which shows how wide the 'carry through' sense is.
senses.whyCN: 仪式只有在被做出来时才存在。这里的 performance 不是娱乐，而是事物得以存在的条件，可见“贯彻到底”这一义项有多宽。

senses.title: The financial results of a business
senses.definition: the financial results of a company, fund, or economy over a period, measured in profit, growth, or return
senses.definitionCN: 公司、基金或经济在一段时间内的财务结果，以利润、增长或回报衡量
senses.example: The fund's performance trailed the index for three quarters.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金连续三个季度的业绩落后于指数。
senses.why: Money is the scoreboard of the market. Performance here is the carrying-through of a strategy expressed as a number that can be compared with rivals.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是市场的记分牌。这里的 performance 是把战略贯彻到底后，用可与对手比较的数字表达出来的结果。

senses.title: Doing that makes what it says
senses.definition: the quality of an utterance or act that brings about what it describes, as when saying 'I promise' is itself the promise
senses.definitionCN: 话语或行为在说出或做出时同时实现其所描述之事的性质，例如说“我保证”本身就是保证
senses.example: The philosopher studied the performative side of promises and apologies.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家研究承诺与道歉的施为性一面。
senses.why: If a promise is completed by being spoken, then the saying is the doing. This sense pushes the 'carry through' idea to its limit: the performance is the only thing there is.
senses.whyCN: 如果承诺因被说出而完成，那么说就是做。这个义项把“贯彻到底”推到极限：表演本身就是唯一存在的东西。

intro.en: Performance comes from perform plus -ance (Latin -antia). Perform is not built on form: it comes from Anglo-French parformer, from Old French parfournir 'to accomplish, complete', literally per- 'thoroughly' + fournir 'to provide, furnish'. The original sense is 'to carry something through to the end'. English added the theatre sense in the 16th century, the machine sense in the 19th, and the linguistic sense in the 20th.
intro.cn: performance 来自 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 并不是由 form 构成的：它来自盎格鲁法语 parformer，再上溯古法语 parfournir“完成、贯彻”，字面是 per-“彻底”+ fournir“提供、供给”。本义是“把某事贯彻到底”。英语在 16 世纪加入戏剧义，19 世纪加入机器义，20 世纪加入语言学义。

items.en: Parfournir means 'to complete, to carry out fully'. The prefix par- is the French form of Latin per- 'thoroughly'; fournir 'to furnish, provide' is from the reconstructed Frankish form *frumjan.
items.cn: parfournir 意为“完成、彻底执行”。前缀 par- 是拉丁 per-“彻底”的法语形式；fournir“供给、提供”出自法兰克语的重构形式 *frumjan。

items.en: English perform first means 'to carry out, accomplish, execute' a task, promise, or duty. The spelling has no connection with form, despite the shared letters.
items.cn: 英语 perform 最早意为“执行、完成、履行”任务、承诺或职责。尽管拼写共享 form 几个字母，它与 form 毫无词源关系。

items.en: The theatre sense develops: to perform a play is to carry the script through into sound and action before an audience.
items.cn: 戏剧义在 16 世纪发展出来：演一部戏，就是把剧本贯彻成观众面前的声与动作。

items.en: Industry applies the word to machines and horses: performance is what an engine or animal can actually deliver under load.
items.cn: 19 世纪工业把这个词用于机器与马匹：performance 是发动机或牲畜在负载下实际能交付的东西。

items.en: Chomsky contrasts performance with competence in linguistics (1965), and management makes performance a measurable target.
items.cn: 20 世纪乔姆斯基在语言学中用 performance 与 competence 相对（1965），管理学则把 performance 变成可测量的指标。

items.en: Form, formal, and formative come from Latin forma 'shape'. Perform has no forma inside it: its fournir is 'provide'. The shared form- is spelling only, so performance is completion, not shaping.
items.cn: form、formal、formative 来自拉丁 forma“形状”。perform 里面没有 forma：它的 fournir 是“提供”。共享的 form- 只是拼写，所以 performance 是完成，不是塑形。

note.en: The first group separates perform's true family from the form trap. The second group compares execution, achievement, a show, and efficiency, the four words most often used in place of performance.
note.cn: 第一组把 perform 真正的词族与 form 陷阱分开。第二组比较执行、成就、演出与效率，这四个词最常被用来替代 performance。

entries.definition: to carry out an action, duty, or work before others. Performance is the noun of that carrying-through.
entries.definitionCN: 执行某项行动、职责或在他人面前呈现作品。performance 是这一贯彻过程的名称。

entries.definition: a person who performs, especially on stage. It names the doer, while performance names the deed or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人。它命名做的人，而 performance 命名行为或其结果。

entries.definition: shape, structure, or a document with blanks. It comes from Latin forma 'shape' and has no connection with perform's fournir 'provide'.
entries.definitionCN: 形状、结构，或带空格的表格。它来自拉丁 forma“形状”，与 perform 的 fournir“提供”毫无关系。

entries.definition: shaping someone's development, as in formative years. It belongs to the forma family, so it is about shaping, not about completing a task.
entries.definitionCN: 塑造人成长的，如“形成期”。它属于 forma 词族，讲的是塑形，不是完成任务。

entries.definition: the act of putting a plan, order, or law into effect. It is close to performance in the task sense but carries no audience or score.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划、命令或法律付诸实施的行为。它在任务义上接近 performance，但不带观众或评分。

entries.definition: something accomplished, especially after effort. It names the result that stands, while performance can name the ongoing doing.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力而完成的事。它命名留下来的结果，而 performance 可以命名正在进行的做。

entries.definition: a public entertainment, or a display. It is the event sense of performance, but it can also mean an insincere display.
entries.definitionCN: 公开的娱乐演出，或展示。它对应 performance 的事件义，但也可以指不真诚的做样子。

entries.definition: the ratio of useful output to the resources used. It is one measured part of performance, not the whole judgement of it.
entries.definitionCN: 有用产出与所耗资源之比。它是 performance 中被测量的一部分，而不是对它的整体判断。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: Old French parfournir, fournir 'provide', the 16th-century stage sense, the 19th-century machine sense, and the form trap.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：古法语 parfournir、fournir“提供”、16 世纪的舞台义、19 世纪的机器义，以及 form 陷阱。

normal.en: Parfournir is 'to complete': a performance is a plan carried through to the end, whether on a stage, in a factory, or under a test load.
normal.cn: parfournir 是“完成”：performance 就是被贯彻到底的计划，无论是在舞台上、车间里，还是在测试负载下。

normal.en: Perform has no form inside it; its fournir means 'provide'. The resemblance to form is a spelling accident.
normal.cn: perform 里面没有 form；它的 fournir 意为“提供”。与 form 的相似只是拼写上的偶然。

normal.en: Theatre gave the word its audience, industry gave it a dial, and linguistics gave it a contrast with competence.
normal.cn: 戏剧给了它观众，工业给了它仪表盘，语言学给了它与“语言能力”的对照。

normal.en: The suffix chain is perform → performer → performance → performative, with -ance naming the act or result.
normal.cn: 后缀链是 perform → performer → performance → performative，其中 -ance 命名行为或结果。

normal.en: A performance review, a live performance, and an engine's performance are the same noun doing three jobs: judgement, event, and limit.
normal.cn: 绩效评估、现场演出与发动机性能，是同一个名词在做三件事：评判、事件与极限。

abstract.en: A score is only a plan for sound; the concert exists for one hour and then cannot be returned to.
abstract.cn: 乐谱只是声音的计划；音乐会存在一小时，然后就再也回不去了。

abstract.en: A machine has no ambition, yet we ask it to perform, as if the dial could be proud.
abstract.cn: 机器没有野心，我们却要求它“表现”，仿佛仪表盘会骄傲。

abstract.en: Saying 'I promise' does not describe the promise; it is the promise, made in the air between two people.
abstract.cn: 说“我保证”并不是在描述承诺；它就是承诺本身，在两个人口之间的空气里做成。

examples.en: The orchestra's performance was broadcast to a million listeners.
examples.cn: 乐团的演出被播给上百万听众。

examples.en: The company reported strong performance in the third quarter.
examples.cn: 公司报告第三季度业绩强劲。

examples.en: The contract requires the performance of the work by June.
examples.cn: 合同要求这项工程在六月前完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破佛曼斯」——演员“破”开剧本，把计划“佛”系地贯彻到底，站在台上做完 → performance 表演；表现；性能（只借音，不表词源）

root: 盎格鲁法语 parformer、古法语 parfournir「完成、贯彻到底」，由 per-「彻底」+ fournir「提供」构成；后缀 -ance（拉丁 -antia）构成名词。核心是「把计划贯彻到底，做到最后」。与 form（拉丁 forma「形状」）只是拼写相似，词根不同；四个主要义项分别是演出、表现、执行、性能。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of performance all describe a plan carried through to the end. What changes is who watches and what counts: an audience, a manager, a contract, a test bench, a grammar, a ritual, a market, or the very act of speaking.
sensesIntro.cn: performance 的九个义项都描述一个被贯彻到底的计划。变化的是谁在看、什么算数：观众、经理、合同、试验台、语法、仪式、市场，还是说话这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plan driven through to the end while others watch and judge the result.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个计划在他人注视与评判下被贯彻到底。

branches.en: THE STAGE AND THE RITE: a work or ceremony carried through before witnesses, and one countable instance of it.
branches.cn: 舞台与仪式：在见证者面前完成的艺术作品或典礼，以及其中可计数的一次。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: a person's or firm's results measured against a standard, including financial results.
branches.cn: 记分牌：个人或公司相对标准的成果，包括财务结果。

branches.en: THE PLAIN DEED: a task or duty actually executed, with no audience beyond the contract.
branches.cn: 朴素的行为：实际执行的任务或职责，除合同外没有别的观众。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S LIMIT: what an engine or system can deliver under load.
branches.cn: 机器的极限：发动机或系统在负载下能交付的东西。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AS DOING: actual speech use in contrast to competence, and utterances that accomplish what they say.
branches.cn: 作为行动的语言：与语言能力相对的实际言语运用，以及说出即做成的话语。

intro.en: Performance is perform plus -ance, from Latin -antia. Perform comes from Old French parfournir, not from form. The family is regular: -er the person, -ance the act or result, -ative the adjective, -ativity the abstract quality.
intro.cn: performance 是 perform 加 -ance（拉丁 -antia）。perform 来自古法语 parfournir，而不是 form。词族很规则：-er 人、-ance 行为或结果、-ative 形容词、-ativity 抽象性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is per- 'thoroughly' and the noun suffix -antia, which forms nouns of state or action. The verb itself is French, from Frankish *frumjan 'to provide'; Latin had no performare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 per-“彻底”与名词后缀 -antia（构成状态或动作名词）。动词本身是法语的，出自法兰克语 *frumjan“提供”；拉丁语并没有 performare 这个动词。

items.meaning: the carrying out of a task, or its public result
items.meaningCN: 任务的执行，或其公开的结果（-ance 动作／结果名词）
items.example: The performance of the pump was tested at low temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这台泵的性能在低温下接受了测试。

items.meaning: to carry out, complete, or present
items.example: The team performed the test twice.
items.exampleCN: 团队把这项测试做了两次。

items.meaning: one who performs, especially on stage
items.meaningCN: 表演的人，尤指舞台上的人（-er 施动者）
items.example: The performer left the stage in silence.
items.exampleCN: 表演者在沉默中离开舞台。

items.meaning: of an utterance that does what it says
items.meaningCN: 指说出即做成之话语的；施为性的（-ative 功能形容词）
items.example: A performative utterance changes the world by being said.
items.exampleCN: 施为性话语通过被说出而改变世界。

items.meaning: the capacity of acts or words to bring about what they name
items.meaningCN: 行为或言语产生其所命名之事的能力；表演性（-ity 性质名词）
items.example: Gender performativity is a key concept in that field.
items.exampleCN: 性别表演性是该领域的一个核心概念。

items.meaningCN: 低于预期标准的表现（under- 低于）
items.example: Underperformance cost the division its bonus.
items.exampleCN: 表现不佳让该部门失去了奖金。

items.meaningCN: 比对手做得更好（out- 超过）
items.example: The fund outperformed its benchmark.
items.exampleCN: 该基金跑赢了基准。

items.meaning: shape or structure; not related to perform
items.meaningCN: 形状或结构；与 perform 不同源
items.example: The form of the roof follows the wind.
items.exampleCN: 屋顶的形状顺着风向。

items.example: They furnished the room before the guests arrived.
items.exampleCN: 客人到达前他们布置好了房间。

latinEntries.meaning: state or action, forming abstract nouns
latinEntries.meaningCN: 状态或动作，构成抽象名词
形状、模子、形式（与 perform 无关）

derivatives.zh: 表演；执行；履行
表演者；执行者
施为性的；表演性的
表演性；施为性
表现不佳

definition_zh: 地形学的；地形上的；与地形测绘有关的；描写地貌起伏的
definition_en: relating to the shape and features of the land surface, or to maps and descriptions that record them
core_image: 测绘员站在雨后的山脊上，把每一道谷地与山头一笔笔画进带等高线的地图
scene: 测绘队在雨后的山脊上架起平板仪，把每一道谷地和山头画进等高线图。 The topographical survey mapped every ridge and valley before the tunnel was designed.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（地形上的、地形学的）；句意为隧道设计之前，地形测量已把每一道山脊与谷地标注到图上。

pos.zh: 形容词：地形上的；地形学的；与地形测绘有关的；描写地貌的

derivatives.zh: 由希腊「地方」与「书写」两个成分加名词词尾构成，义为「地形；地形学；地形描述」
由名词加形容词词尾构成，与「地形上的」基本同义，技术文献中更常见
由名词加表示「从事者」的词尾构成，义为「地形测绘员；地形描述者」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在地形方面；从地形上看」
共享表示「地方」的第一个成分，加表示「名字」的成分，义为「地名」
由地名一词加学科名词词尾构成，义为「地名学」
共享表示「地方」的第一个成分，加表示「学问」的成分，义为「拓扑学」

senses.title: Relating to the shape of the land
senses.definition: concerning the physical relief of an area, its heights, slopes and depressions
senses.definitionCN: 指与某地区地表的起伏形态有关，包括高度、坡度与低洼处
senses.example: The topographical features of the valley decide where rain water collects.
senses.exampleCN: 谷地的地形特征决定雨水往哪里汇集。
senses.why: The Greek elements name a place and the act of writing it down, so the adjective first describes land that has been described.
senses.whyCN: 希腊成分一为「地方」、一为「书写」，因此这个形容词最初指「被描写下来的土地」。

senses.title: Belonging to a topographic map
senses.definition: shown on a map by contour lines, hachures or relief shading
senses.definitionCN: 指以等高线、晕滃或晕渲等方式表现在地图上
senses.example: The topographical map shows a steep drop beside the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 地形图上显示溪边有一处陡降。
senses.why: Once surveyors drew relief, the adjective moved from the land itself to the sheet that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 测量员把起伏画下来之后，这个词就从土地本身转到承载它的图纸上。

senses.title: Of regional anatomy
senses.definition: describing how structures are arranged within one region of the body
senses.definitionCN: 指描述身体某一区域内各结构的位置关系
senses.example: Topographical anatomy divides the neck into named triangles.
senses.exampleCN: 局部解剖学把颈部划分成若干具名三角区。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the mapping idea: a body region is charted like terrain.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了制图的想法：身体的一个区域也像地形一样被分区标注。

senses.title: Descriptive of a landscape in words
senses.definition: giving a detailed written account of the visible shape of a place
senses.definitionCN: 指用文字细致描写一个地方可见的形貌
senses.example: The novel opens with a topographical passage about the estuary.
senses.exampleCN: 小说以一段描写河口地貌的文字开篇。
senses.why: Writing a place down was the original meaning, and prose kept that literal sense alive.
senses.whyCN: 把地方写下来本是原义，散文让这层字面意思延续下来。

senses.title: Contrasted with political maps
senses.definition: showing natural relief rather than borders and administrative units
senses.definitionCN: 指表现自然起伏而非边界与行政单元
senses.example: A topographical map ignores provincial borders.
senses.exampleCN: 地形图不标省界。
senses.why: Surveying separated natural form from jurisdiction, and the adjective marks the natural side.
senses.whyCN: 测绘把自然形态与管辖范围分开，这个形容词标记的是自然那一面。

senses.title: Of terrain as a constraint
senses.definition: describing ground conditions that affect travel, construction or drainage
senses.definitionCN: 指影响通行、施工或排水的地面条件
senses.example: Topographical difficulties delayed the bridge by a full season.
senses.exampleCN: 地形上的困难使桥梁工程整整延期一季。
senses.why: Engineers treat terrain as a limit, so the adjective names the obstacle rather than the science.
senses.whyCN: 工程师把地形当作限制条件，于是这个词指障碍而非学科。

senses.title: Of relative height among peaks
senses.definition: in geography, describing the height of a summit above its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 地理学中指山峰高出周围地面的程度
senses.example: Topographical prominence decides whether a summit counts as a separate peak.
senses.exampleCN: 地形突出度决定一座山峰是否算作独立山峰。
senses.why: Relief is measured vertically as well as drawn horizontally, and prominence is the vertical reading.
senses.whyCN: 起伏除横向描绘之外还要纵向度量，突出度就是纵向读数。

senses.title: Figurative: the shape of a field of knowledge
senses.definition: used for the overall arrangement of ideas, as if they had heights and hollows
senses.definitionCN: 比喻思想观念的整体分布，仿佛它们也有高低起伏
senses.example: The lecture gives a topographical view of the whole debate.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座给出整场论争的版图式概览。
senses.why: Mapping moved from land to ideas, keeping the sense of an outline drawn from above.
senses.whyCN: 制图从土地移到观念，仍保留「从上往下勾出轮廓」的意思。

intro.en: Topographical joins Greek topos, a place, with graphein, to write or scratch, through the Latin noun topographia, a written description of a place. English took the noun as topography and added the adjective ending -ical.
intro.cn: 这个形容词把希腊语中表示「地方」的词与表示「书写、刻画」的词连在一起，经拉丁语中意为「对某地的文字描述」的名词进入英语；英语先借入名词，再加形容词词尾构成形容词。

items.en: Topos meant a place or a region, the spot that a speaker or writer points to.
items.cn: 这个词指一个地方或一片区域，即说话人或写作者所指的那一处。

items.en: Graphein meant to write or scratch, and it supplies the second half of many names of descriptive sciences.
items.cn: 这个词意为书写、刻画，是许多描述性学科名称的后半部分。

items.en: Latin combined the two Greek elements into a noun for a written account of a place; the term belongs to early modern Latin, and its first use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 拉丁语把两个希腊成分合成一个名词，指对某地的文字记述；该词属于近代早期拉丁语，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: English adopted the noun first for the description of a district and later for the district's relief itself.
items.cn: 英语先借入这个名词指对某一地区的描述，后来指该地区的地形起伏本身。

items.en: The adjective spread with systematic surveying and was common by the nineteenth century; its precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词随系统测绘的兴起而扩散，到十九世纪已很常见，确切首见年份不确定。

items.en: Surveying, anatomy and engineering each took the adjective for the charting of their own ground.
items.cn: 测绘、解剖与工程各自借这个词来指称本领域「地盘」的图绘。

note.en: The first group shares the place element or the adjective ending; the second group names other ways of talking about the shape of the ground.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「地方」的成分或形容词词尾；第二组是谈论地面形态的其他说法。

entries.definition: The shorter adjective, preferred in technical writing, especially in American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的形容词，技术写作中更常用，尤其在美国用法里。

entries.definition: The noun for the relief of an area or the study and mapping of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指一个地区的起伏，或对它的研究与测绘。

entries.definition: A person who surveys and describes the surface of the land.
entries.definitionCN: 指测绘并描述地表形态的人。

entries.definition: A place name, built from the same first element with a word for name.
entries.definitionCN: 指地名，由同一个第一个成分与表示「名字」的成分构成。

entries.definition: The mathematical study of shape that survives stretching, with a different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 数学中对拉伸后仍不变的形状性质的研究，第二个成分不同。

entries.definition: The variation in height of a land surface, the thing a topographic map draws.
entries.definitionCN: 指地表高低起伏的变化，正是地形图所绘制的内容。

entries.definition: The ground considered as a surface to cross or build on.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为通行或施工对象的地面。

entries.definition: A specific natural feature such as a ridge, valley or plain.
entries.definitionCN: 指山脊、谷地、平原等具体的自然形态。

entries.definition: Relating to the making and design of maps in general.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与地图制作与设计有关。

entries.definition: Relating to the scientific study of how landforms are formed.
entries.definitionCN: 指与研究地貌如何形成的学科有关。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the two Greek elements: a place plus the act of writing it down.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着两个希腊成分展开：一个地方，加上把它写下来的动作。

normal.en: Place plus writing: topographical means the land has been written down.
normal.cn: 地方加书写：这个形容词的意思就是「土地被写成了图」。

normal.en: Contour lines are its signature look; a topographic map is relief made legible.
normal.cn: 等高线是它最典型的样子；地形图就是把起伏变得可读。

normal.en: A topographic map shows hills; a political map shows borders.
normal.cn: 地形图画出山丘，政区图画出边界。

normal.en: Topographical anatomy charts the body as if it were terrain.
normal.cn: 局部解剖学把身体当作地形来分区标注。

normal.en: Engineers list topographical difficulties when the ground itself is the problem.
normal.cn: 工程师列出的地形困难，指问题出在地面本身。

abstract.en: Every map is an argument about which features on the ground deserve to be drawn.
abstract.cn: 每一张地图都是一场争论：地面上哪些特征值得被画出来。

abstract.en: Relief is height turned into a language of lines.
abstract.cn: 起伏就是把高度翻译成一套线条语言。

abstract.en: To describe a place is already to choose a viewpoint above it.
abstract.cn: 描述一个地方，等于已经替它选好了一个居高临下的视角。

examples.en: The topographical survey mapped the flood plain before the dam was approved.
examples.cn: 大坝获批之前，地形测量已把洪泛平原测绘成图。

examples.en: Topographical maps show relief, not provincial borders.
examples.cn: 地形图表现起伏，不表现省界。

examples.en: Topographical anatomy helps a surgeon plan where to cut.
examples.cn: 局部解剖学帮助外科医生规划下刀的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「托坡格拉菲扣」——托着坡度、按格画线的一叠图，一张地形图：地形上的、地形学的

root: 希腊语 topos「地方」加 graphein「书写、刻画」，经拉丁语 topographia「对某地的记述」进入英语；形容词由名词加 -ical 构成，早期确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a place being written down to the map, the body, the building site and finally the shape of an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「把地方写下来」出发，依次走向地图、身体、工地，最后落到论争的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surveyor on a wet ridge, drawing every hollow and summit onto a sheet of contour lines.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后的山脊上，测绘员把每一处低洼与山头画进一张等高线图。

branches.en: THE LAND DESCRIBED: spoken or written description of visible shape, the oldest use of the root.
branches.cn: 被描写的大地：对可见形貌的口头或书面描述，这是词根最古老的用法。

branches.en: THE MAP ITSELF: contour lines and natural features, set against borders and administrative units.
branches.cn: 地图本身：等高线与自然要素，与边界和行政单元相对。

branches.en: THE BODY AS GROUND: anatomy charts regions of the body the way a survey charts terrain.
branches.cn: 把身体当地面：解剖学像测绘地形那样标注身体分区。

branches.en: THE GROUND AS OBSTACLE OR MEASURE: terrain slows a project, and prominence ranks a summit.
branches.cn: 地面成为障碍或量度：地形拖慢工程，突出度给山峰排名。

branches.en: THE SHAPE OF IDEAS: a field of knowledge is described as if it had heights and hollows.
branches.cn: 观念的形态：一片知识被描述得仿佛也有高低起伏。

intro.en: Both halves of the word are Greek; Latin supplied the combined noun, and English added a compound adjective ending.
intro.cn: 这个词的两半都出自希腊语；拉丁语提供了合成名词，英语又加上了复合形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are borrowings of the Greek compound rather than native Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 列出的拉丁形式是从希腊语借入的合成词，并非本土拉丁词根。

items.example: It is the first element in topography and toponym.
items.exampleCN: 它是「地形」与「地名」的第一个成分。

items.example: It supplies the second element in geography and biography.
items.exampleCN: 它是「地理」与「传记」的第二个成分。

items.example: It names a descriptive discipline or a style of writing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述性学科或书写体式的名称。

items.meaning: a written description of a place
items.example: The Latin noun carried both the place and the writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词同时带着「地方」与「书写」。

items.meaning: relief of an area; its mapping
items.meaningCN: 一个地区的起伏；对其测绘
items.example: English shortened and naturalised the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁名词缩短并本土化。

items.example: It forms topographical from topography.
items.exampleCN: 它由名词构成这个形容词。

items.meaning: one who surveys or describes terrain
items.example: The agent ending names the person who does the writing.
items.exampleCN: 表示施动者的词尾指从事这项书写的人。

items.example: The shorter ending is common in technical writing.
items.exampleCN: 较短的词尾在技术写作中更常见。

items.example: The second element means name rather than writing.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分意为「名字」而非「书写」。

items.meaning: study of shape under continuous change
items.meaningCN: 研究连续变化下形状性质的学问
items.example: The second element means study or discourse.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分意为「学问、论述」。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊「地方」与「书写」加名词词尾构成，义为「地形；地形学」
由名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「地形的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在地形方面」
由名词加表示施动者的词尾构成，义为「地形测绘员」
共享表示「地方」的成分，加表示「名字」的成分，义为「地名」
由地名一词加学科词尾构成，义为「地名学」
共享表示「地方」的成分，加表示「学问」的成分，义为「拓扑学」
由表示「地方」的希腊成分构成的构词成分，用于构成地点类术语
